acceptance_criteria:
Platform Deployment

  1. A live, branded training platform accessible online;
  2. Includes core LMS functionality: user registration, dashboard, course navigation, media playback, and content progress tracking;
  3. Stable hosting with ≥ 99% uptime, mobile-responsive design, and average page load <3 seconds.

Course Content (Quantitative Standards)

  1. Each course contains a minimum of 3 missions, each mission with:
  2. At least 15 pages of written content;
  3. Minimum of 4 quizzes (12 total per course);
  4. 2 practical submission exercises per course;
  5. 1 peer-reviewed assignment per course;
  6. Estimated minimum 25 hours of total time to complete each course;
  7. All content is clear, original, and written in professional English.

Instructional Quality

  1. All modules follow a consistent 4-stage structure;
  2. Content includes a mix of text, visuals, and video;
  3. High production standards: clean design, quality audio/video, edited and reviewed before publishing;
  4. Designed to be beginner-friendly yet rigorous, suitable for early-stage technical founders;

User Experience

  1. Functional platform tested across major browsers and mobile;
  2. Navigation is intuitive; maximum 2 clicks to access any module;
  3. Users can register, log in, track progress, and resume lessons without error.

Brand Consistency

  1. Cardano ecosystem branding is consistently applied across the platform UI, course headers, and visual media.
description:
As the foundational step of this initiative, we’ll deploy a dedicated instance of our white label training platform, fully branded for the Cardano ecosystem. This custom platform will serve as the central hub for onboarding non-English-speaking technical founders, enabling them to access tailored training content and tools aligned with Cardano’s unique protocols and community values. The Cardano-branded interface ensures a seamless experience for users while reinforcing ecosystem identity throughout the learning journey.

We'll prepare the internal structure of the platform with Course #1: Product Market Fit and Course #2: How to Launch on Cardano. Both programs will be developed in English, at this stage, and will be included on the platform.

Each course follows our proven instructional framework across four stages:

  1. Learn the Concept – foundational theory through expert-led lessons;
  2. Self-Study – independent review of curated content and real-world examples;
  3. Test Knowledge – quizzes and checkpoint assessments;
  4. Apply to Your Business Idea – practical assignments that bridge theory to action.
title: Cardano Platform Launch

acceptance_criteria:
Translation Scope & Standards

  1. Full translation of platform UI and both courses into Simplified Chinese.
  2. Minimum translation scope includes:
  3. Platform interface (UI elements, navigation, user prompts);
  4. ~45 pages of course content (from Milestone 1: 3 missions × 15 pages/course × 2 courses);
  5. 12 quizzes, 4 submission exercises, 2 peer review tasks;
  6. Translation reviewed and validated by at least 2 native Chinese-speaking professional translators, each with technical background.
  7. Translators must meet professional standards: minimum 2 years of translation experience or equivalent certifications.
  8. All translated content reviewed using a 4-point QA checklist:
  9. Accuracy of technical terms;
  10. Natural fluency in modern Chinese;
  11. Cultural relevance and tone;
  12. Functional UI display.

Original Chinese-Language Content Development

  1. Minimum of:
  2. 1 new video tutorial (≥5 minutes, Chinese narration or subtitles)
  3. 2 written guides (≥750 words each)
  4. 1 integration walkthrough (step-by-step, with code examples)
  5. Content developed in collaboration with at least 1 active member of the Chinese-speaking Cardano community (documented contribution).
  6. All new content peer-reviewed for technical accuracy and alignment with Cardano's current ecosystem tools.
description:
Develop materials tailored specifically for technical founders new to the ecosystem. This includes guided tutorials, ecosystem overviews, and integration walkthroughs aimed at driving real adoption and code contributions. Both courses and newly created content will be professionally translated into Chinese, making it fully accessible to our initial target audience and ready for program rollout.

To ensure cultural and linguistic relevance, we actively engaged with the existing Chinese-speaking Cardano community, joining key social media groups, identifying trusted influencers, and tracking relevant events. This groundwork helped align content with actual user needs and ecosystem expectations.
title: Cardano Chinese-Language Content

acceptance_criteria:
Targeting & Outreach Execution

  1. Outreach strategy includes at least:
  2. 3 Cardano-aligned communication channels (e.g., forums, Discords, Telegram groups);
  3. 1 outbound campaign via Infrastructure's sourcing tool using a founder intent profile.
  4. All outbound messages align with Cardano values, use consistent branding, and include program links.

Founder Selection Criteria

  1. All 15 founders must meet eligibility requirements:
  2. Background in software or blockchain development;
  3. A defined startup idea or working prototype;
  4. Willingness to participate in structured program feedback.
  5. Founders verified via public profiles, GitHub links, or ecosystem references.

Program Engagement Quality

  1. All founders fully onboarded to the platform and assigned learning paths;
  2. Progress logged for each founder across the four-stage curriculum;
  3. Completion metrics recorded per stage:
  4. Stage 1-2: ≥80% lesson engagement;
  5. Stage 3: 100% quiz submission;
  6. Stage 4: ≥1 practical application submitted per founder.

Feedback Quality Standards

  1. Net Promoter Score (NPS) collected after Week 2 for both founder groups;
  2. Minimum 80 NPS;
  3. Feedback surveys include at least 3 open-ended qualitative questions;
  4. NPS data compiled into a structured report with:
  5. Score breakdown;
  6. Thematic summary of open responses;
  7. Action items derived from feedback.

Project Development Snapshot

  1. Each of the 15 founders must submit:
  2. 1-paragraph summary of their current project idea;
  3. One of the following: GitHub repo link, architecture sketch, or MVP spec doc;
  4. These submissions logged in the platform and included in the reviewer report.
description:
We'll collaborate with members of the Cardano community to identify channels and gather recommendations for high-potential applicants into the program. This coordination helped align our outreach with the ecosystem’s active contributors and trusted networks.

In parallel, we created a detailed messaging and targeting profile designed for Infrastructure’s founder-sourcing platform. This profile identifies developers showing clear 'build intent', measured through public repos, community engagement, and startup indicators, and proactively invites them into the program.

With open enrollment in place, we'll have the first two groups, the first five founders, and then ten founders, who will join the program. These initial groups provide an early opportunity to gather structured feedback through Net Promoter Score (NPS) surveys and track progress metrics, such as completion rates for each stage of the curriculum.

All relevant participation data is logged on the platform and available to milestone reviewers for transparent evaluation.

Initial program activation:

  1. Launch targeted outreach campaigns using Cardano community channels and Infrastructure’s founder-sourcing platform;
  2. Apply a detailed targeting profile to identify technical founders with verifiable build intent (public GitHub activity, startup affiliations, active participation in blockchain communities);
  3. Enroll and onboard the first 15 founders, in two waves:
  4. Wave 1: 5 founders;
  5. Wave 2: 10 founders.
  6. Collect structured participant feedback and track early-stage learning outcomes;
  7. Log all relevant data for transparent milestone review.
title: Outbound Messaging, Targeting & Initial Founder Engagement

acceptance_criteria:
Program Graduates

  1. Minimum 40 founders complete the program, defined as:
  2. Full participation in all 4 curriculum stages;
  3. Submission of the final project/application aligned with Cardano;
  4. Completion of feedback surveys;
  5. Demonstrated activity (e.g., repo commits, integration steps, on-chain interaction).
  6. Graduation requires achieving:
  7. ≥80% mission completion;
  8. 100% quiz submission rate;
  9. Final project submission with either a demo, repo, or walkthrough doc.

Final Report (Quality Standards)

  1. 6+ pages professionally formatted PDF report, including:
  2. Program overview and methodology;
  3. Outreach and selection process summary;
  4. Participation stats (total applicants, accepted, completed);
  5. NPS and feedback breakdown;
  6. Project showcase (screenshots, links, or summaries);
  7. Lessons learned + recommendations for future Cardano founder support;
  8. Report reviewed by at least 1 external Cardano ecosystem participant before publication

Final Closeout Video

  1. 3–5 minute professionally edited video;
  2. Includes:
  3. Program highlights;
  4. Founder testimonials;
  5. Screenshots or clips from the platform;
  6. Subtitles in English and Chinese;
  7. Hosted publicly on a shareable video platform (e.g., YouTube, IPFS).

Performance Metrics Tracked

  1. Platform logs show:
  2. Enrollment totals;
  3. Stage-by-stage completion rates;
  4. NPS scores;
  5. Founder activity (e.g., repo links, comments, submissions).
  6. Graduation and engagement stats shared in final report and available as CSV or PDF.
description:
Progress will be measured by the number of founders who complete the program and meet our defined performance metrics, such as code contributions, engagement levels, and NPS scores. Each graduate represents a consistent unit cost, allowing for predictable scaling and efficient resource allocation.

This milestone captures the final delivery, graduation outcomes, and ecosystem contribution of the program. It includes:

  • Scaled outreach and founder onboarding beyond the initial 15 participants;
  • Graduation of founders who meet defined completion and performance criteria;
  • Collection and analysis of program-wide metrics: enrollment, engagement, NPS, and project maturity;
  • Publication of a professional-grade final report and closeout video for accountability and knowledge sharing.
title: Scale Outreach & Closeout

description:
Activities:

Conduct deep research on decentralized governance models and human rights-focused tokenomics.

Collaborate with blockchain experts, human rights advocates, and economists to explore the potential of a Human Rights Token.

Complete the project plan outline for approval.

Explicit research questions to guide the comparative analysis of governance models would include:

  • What are the key features of successful decentralised governance models in ensuring equity, transparency, and accountability?
  • How do various models address power imbalances and ensure marginalised voices are included in decision-making?
  • What metrics or indicators are most effective for measuring the impact of governance models on social justice or advocacy outcomes?
  • What lessons can be drawn from failures in decentralised governance projects, particularly those involving large participation?
  • Which governance mechanisms (e.g., quadratic voting, token-weighted voting, or reputation systems) are most appropriate for scaling human rights-focused initiatives?

  • What alternate systems are being evolved to further define decentralised governance?


Deliverables:

Whitepaper on DAO governance models for social impact and potentials for token design, including these critical aspects for thorough conceptualisation:

  • Comparative analysis of governance models tailored to Amnesty's global human rights advocacy needs.
  • Detailed exploration of tokenomics challenges and mitigation strategies, such as regulatory compliance or potential misuse.
  • Inclusion of specific use cases or scenarios that align with the Amnesty mission and are actionable within campaign strategic deliverables, including demonstrating how the DAO and token design would work in practice.
  • Project plan documenting timelines, budgets, and phased deliverables for stakeholder validation.
title: Research & Conceptualization (Month 1-3)

acceptance_criteria:
The core smart contracts for the DAO governance system and the human rights token will be designed.

The governance smart contracts are coded and tested, Providing clear evidence of successful testing of the smart contracts with sample scenarios. Success metrics include for instance:

  • Accuracy: Outputs (e.g., token rewards, staking calculations) match the predefined tokenomics model under all tested scenarios.
  • Functionality: all core contract functions execue without errors or unintended consequences.
  • Security: Contracts withstand common vulnerabilities.
  • Scalability: Contracts perform efficiently under stress tests simulating high user activity.

The human rights token's utility, distribution mechanism, and reward system are defined. 

Approval from technical reviewers after a thorough audit, Including audit results from technical reviewers, outlining the methodology and any resolved issues.

  • Ensuring the deliverables include documentation for token utility and its long-term sustainability.
description:
Develop a comprehensive tokenomics model to simulate the distribution of rewards, governance influence, and long-term sustainability of the Human Rights Token.

Define specific metrics and parameters to ensure reproducibility, including for instance:

  • Reward distribution rates based on user activity (e.g., advocacy contributions, voting).
  • Stake-to-vote ratios and governance influence weights.
  • Inflation or deflation mechanisms over defined timeframes.

Use tools like simulation software to test various models of token issuance, staking, and redemption. Model how different actions translate into token rewards.

Deliverables:

  • Tokenomics model and simulation results. Documentation of how simulation software was used to model token issuance, staking, and redemption, with a detailed methodology section in the simulation documentation to enhance transparency.
  • Explanation of how different actions translate into token rewards within the simulation, including, where possible, user scenarios or test cases to demonstrate how token rewards and governance models work in real-life simulations.
  • Detailed outputs from the simulation results, such as data visualisations or insights into token sustainability and governance influence.
  • Providing clear evidence of successful testing of the smart contracts with sample scenarios, including metrics for execution of smart contracts without errors, security and vulnerability testing confirmations, and accurate token issuance, redemption, and reward allocation as per the model specifications.
  • Include audit results from technical reviewers, outlining the methodology and any resolved issues.
  • Ensure the deliverables include documentation for token utility and its long-term sustainability.

The audit procedure will be based on the measureable and time-bound milestones, including a timeline or checklist for resolving audit issues to demonstrate readiness for the next phase. We will track issue resolution using Asana, with weekly updates on progress and re-testing.

Asana software project management tool will detail progress for each milestone with updated budget tracking. Progress will be checked against defined deliverables at each stage.
title: Tokenomics Modeling & Simulation

acceptance_criteria:
A functional MVP prototype of the DAO platform is built for a private user group, and a user testing phase is completed with feedback from key stakeholders, detailing how:

- Supporters can create proposals, vote, and engage in discussions. Feedback from the focus user group and stakeholders is incorporated, showing how their inputs influenced platform refinements.

- Results from security and scalability testing are detailed, demonstrating that the platform can handle real-world usage scenarios, including measurable metrics or benchmarks for security and scalability tests (e.g., maximum load capacity, response time under stress, and vulnerability testing).

- Evidence clearly illustrates the platform's ability to support proposals, voting, and discussions effectively.

- A detailed roadmap in included for resolving any issues identified during user testing, and including a plan to retest the platform post-issue resolution.

- Highlighting specific steps taken to ensure the DAO’s scalability for larger deployments in the future.


To ensure transparency and credibility:

Publish the MVP codebase, documentation, and testing results on a GitHub repository for public access.

Include a comprehensive README file detailing:

Key functionalities of the DAO.

Steps for replicating or testing the MVP.

Uploaded user feedback reports and results from security and scalability testing as above to the repository.
description:
Build a prototype DAO on Cardano and test core functionalities (voting, proposal submission, token rewards).

Develop initial voting, governance, and token distribution mechanisms. Conduct small-scale testing with a focus group from Amnesty International.

Provide detailed documentation of the MVP functionalities, such as:

  • Step-by-step explanations of the voting, proposal submission, and token distribution processes, including specific examples and user scenarios from the focus group to illustrate functionality.
  • Evidence of how these functionalities meet the intended goals.
  • Test cases or scenarios showcasing the DAO in action, particularly with the focus group from Amnesty International.
  • Demonstration of the integration of token rewards and governance mechanisms in practical use cases.
  • Details on how feedback from the focus group influenced the final DAO design, and
  • Providing clear evidence of the token reward system's alignment with governance goals, including data or visualizations.
title: MVP DAO Development & Testing

description:
FOR REVIEWERS: Prior to reading the milestones, we request that you review relevant definitions and clarifications in this Proposal Clarifications Document. 

USE OF FUNDS:

The full Catalyst funding requested through this proposal will be allocated to fulfill the publisher’s contractual guarantee licensing fee, as outlined in their confidential agreement with Book.io. As stated in the proposal, this funding will be disbursed with complete transparency, and all transactions to the publisher will be made accessible for review by Catalyst Fund auditors, ensuring accountability and alignment with Catalyst’s funding standards.

All activities delivered across these milestones—including technical integration, reporting, education, and ecosystem activation—are directly related to and required for operationalizing, validating, and sustaining the licensed catalog on Cardano.

PRIMARY PURPOSE: Accumulate 75,000 ADA toward the initial publisher rights acquisition payment (as stated in original proposal: "The full Catalyst funding requested through this proposal will be allocated to fulfill the publisher's contractual guarantee licensing fee").

PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES: Deliver foundational project components while preserving funds for publisher payment.

MILESTONE OUTPUTS:

A.) Dedicated Catalyst wallet and funding record showing Milestone 1 disbursement amount (80% of 75,000 ADA) reserved for rights acquisition (minus documented related administrative costs).

B.) ONIX ingestion database tables and configuration setup for receiving publisher ONIX feed data including key metadata fields such as title, author, description, pricing, rights, and identifiers (ISBN).

C.) ONIX schema validation and mapping compatibility package confirming alignment with ONIX XML file structure. Establishing elements 2 and 3 are core to the proposal’s execution, as it is not possible to onboard the catalog without the ONIX developments.

D.) Project Progress Page with milestone tracking, community communication sections, and a summary of existing ONIX ingestion capabilities and readiness for post-acquisition catalog integration.
title: Rights Acquisition Fund Accumulation & Platform Enhancement

description:
CAP will use features from cardano-node, db-sync, and APIs to extract data from the cardano network. CAP needs to extract data (output 1) from the Cardano network to structure it in a triplestore to support semantic search. In this sense, the data must be aligned (output 2) according to the ontology delivered on Milestone 1. The data extraction, transformation and loading into the knowledge base delivered on Milestone 1 will be performed by ETLs pipelines (output 3). We will create tests (output 4) to assert if the implemented mechanisms are performing according to the expected behaviour. That is, extracted data is correctly retrieved and injected in the Knowledge Base according to the ontology definition.

Contractor Agreement

  • Intellectual Property (IP) Clause:
  • Clearly defines the transfer of IP rights from the supplier to Cardano founders.
  • Includes a comprehensive licensing clause ensuring smooth transfer of all delivered IP.
  • Addresses perpetual, territorial and paid/royalty-free usage.
  • Confidentiality Clause:
  • Ensures protection of proprietary information disclosed during the agreement.
  • Covers non-disclosure obligations, permitted disclosures, and breach consequences.
  • Jurisdiction and Governing Law:
  • Specifies England and Wales as the applicable neutral jurisdiction.
  • Allows enforceability across multiple international locations.
  • Supplier Engagement Flexibility:
  • Provides a framework allowing Cardano founders to contract with suppliers globally.
  • Contains clear terms for contract duration, termination, and renewals.


MSA between provider and clients

  • Scope of Services:
  • Link to Statement of Work/Service Order clearly defines the scope of services to be provided by the provider.
  • Includes flexibility to add or remove services as needed.
  • Non-Hire Clause:
  • Strictly prohibits clients from poaching project personnel during and for a defined period after the engagement.
  • Defines penalties or remedies in case of breach.
  • Testing Period Clause:
  • Specifies an initial testing period for deliverables, means of remedy and further limiting of responsibility after lapse of testing period.
  • Jurisdiction and Governing Law:
  • Designates England and Wales as the neutral jurisdiction.
  • Termination:
  • Includes clear terms for termination rights and notice periods.


SLA

  • Service Level Objectives (SLOs):
  • Specifies measurable performance metrics (e.g., uptime, response time).
  • Defines key performance indicators (KPIs) with clear targets.
  • Roles and Responsibilities:
  • Clearly outlines responsibilities of both parties to avoid ambiguity.
  • Defines escalation processes for service failures.
  • Remedies for Non-Compliance:
  • Details penalties, credits, or remedial actions if service levels are not met.
  • Specifies reporting obligations and review mechanisms.
  • Jurisdiction and Governing Law:
  • Ensures legal governance under England and Wales jurisdiction.
  • Provides clarity on liability limitations and indemnities.


﻿NDA

  • Mutual Obligation:
  • Covers confidentiality obligations for both parties equally.
  • Ensures mutual understanding of shared proprietary information.
  • Definition of Confidential Information:
  • Provides a detailed definition of what constitutes confidential information.
  • Specifies exclusions, including publicly available information or disclosures to advisors.
  • Exemptions Clause:
  • Clearly outlines circumstances under which disclosure is permitted (e.g., legal obligations, advisors).
  • Duration and Survival of Obligations:
  • Specifies the duration of confidentiality obligations even after contract termination.
  • Defines a reasonable timeframe - 3 years from the sharing of last proprietary information.
  • Jurisdiction and Governing Law:
  • Establishes England and Wales as the neutral jurisdiction.

acceptance_criteria:
1) The discovery process report provides an actionable insight to begin development:

  • At least 10 developers have been contacted.
  • Survey responses follow a pre-defined survey format.
  • A concrete use case has been selected based on responses.

2) ﻿The project’s repository and source-code are suitable for feature development:

  • Substrate template primitives (such as consensus pallet, frame runtime, and chain spec) are clearly defined.
  • Rust code passes formatting and linting checks (cargo fmt and cargo clippy show no warnings), ensuring adherence to style conventions and best practices.
  • The repository includes developer instructions for contributions, release procedures, and bug reporting.
  • A CI pipeline on GitHub Actions runs automated checks on each pull request.
  • Documentation explains the project structure.
description:
1) Discovery process report: A report that includes a description of the activities and outcomes of the discovery process. This process involves reaching out to developer teams in the Cardano ecosystem, explaining the goals of the project and asking them to complete a small survey with feedback. The results will be used to define the concrete use-case to implement.

2) Substrate node client scaffold: An off-the-shelf Substrate client using the latest available template. This scaffold will contains generic artifacts required to begin with feature development. This scaffold will be manifested as a Rust project in a public repository in Github.
title: Project Scaffolding

acceptance_criteria:
1) A developer is able to use the initial customized Substrate node to build features on top:

  • The provided codebase includes a consensus mechanism, a basic ledger model and runtime, a storage mechanism and basic schema.
  • A developer can clone, compile and execute the Substrate node without extra modifications to the codebase.
  • The Substrate node should be able to initialize runtime, establish network connectivity and synchronize with other peers.

2) The implementation process is documented and available for the public use:

  • The public can recognize in the documents the key design decisions regarding consensus, ledger and storage
  • The public can follow each step of the implementation process through the log in chronological order.
  • The public can compare expected outputs and interpret results to verify successful execution.
description:
1) Initial Substrate node customizations: A Substrate client that will include the required high-level customizations. This changes will include the selection of a consensus mechanism, a ledger model and storage structure. This client won't perform any real functions but will be able to bootstrap and connect to peers, serving as a robust foundation for further development.

2) Dev activity log: A detailed log of the development activities that were required for the Substrate client customization. This log will serve as guidance for new developers wishing to understand the process with the goal of implementing their own versions.
title: Generic Substrate Chain

acceptance_criteria:
1) The customized Substrate client should participate of the Partnerchain consensus

  • A developer is able to clone and compile the Substrate node without extra modifications to the codebase
  • The Rust project should compile and the binary executables for the Substrate node should be generated. This is the binary that allows a user to start the Substrate node.
  • A developer can use the example Partnerchain configuration and instructions to join their node to the Partnerchain
  • The binary executable is able to start and the required bootstrapping procedures are executed. This procedures include loading the existing chain data, loading the runtime and attempting to connect to other nodes in the network. The evidence for these steps is shown in the terminal output of the process.

2) The L1 governance contracts are available to be used by developers

  • The provided codebase includes parametrized scripts that can be used via common developer tooling (eg: Aiken) to generate concrete instances of the scripts.
  • A particular version of the scripts parametrized for an examples partnerchain can be found on-chain as a reference scripts. This will allow further Cardano transactions to reference the script.
  • The developer can follow the included instructions to execute the Cardano transactions that would include a particular entity in the partnerchain block-producer committee.

3) The provided dev log and instructions are sufficient to understand and replicate the applied customizations

  • A section in the documentation provides human readable content describing the activity of the developers that worked on this milestone.
  • The described activity shows the steps that were required to turn the generic Substrate node into one that integrates with the partnerchain consensus mechanism.

4) The usage instructions allows a developer to interact with the system developed during this milestone.

  • The instructions includes the steps required to compile the provided codebase.
  • The instructions includes the steps to execute the L1 contracts that allows an operator to join a partnerchain.
  • The instructions includes the steps required to bootstrap the Substrate node with the corresponding documentation (a.ka.: start the node).
description:
1) Partnerchain SDK integration: Our customized Substrate client that is now integrated with the Partnerchain SDK. This means that the node will be able to participate in the consensus mechanism by providing a valid Partnerchain configuration and keys.

2) Governance contracts on L1: An instance of the governance contracts for a particular partnerchain deployed in the Cardano preview network. This governance contracts will validate the Pools operators that are able to participate of the Partnerchain consensus.

3) Dev activity log: A detailed log of the development activities that were required for the Substrate client customization. This log will serve as guidance for new developers wishing to understand the process with the goal of implementing their own versions.

4) Usage instructions: Detailed instructions on how to prepare the required Partnerchain contracts and how to run our custom client as part of the partnerchain.
title: Cardano Integration

acceptance_criteria:
1) Documentation clearly outlines the key design decisions and technical specifications regarding features associated with the use-case defined in MS1 for the public usage.

2) A developer is able to use the customized Substrate node to build features on top:

  • The provided codebase for the Substrate client includes the required modifications specific to the defined use-case.
  • A developer can clone, compile and execute the Substrate client without extra modifications to the codebase.
  • The Substrate client successfully initializes, and should be able to execute use-case-specific transactions.

3) The implementation process is documented and available for the public use:

  • The public can identify the necessary steps to replicate the implementation process with the necessary customizations.
  • The public can compare expected outputs and interpret results to verify successful execution.
description:
1) Use-case specific documentation: A document that explains what are the required features and implementation details to develop the use-case that was defined during the discovery process in MS1.

2) Use-case specific features: The set of features that transforms our generic Substrate client into one that is specialized to fulfill a specific goal (oracle, game, etc). The concrete set of features to develop will depend on the outcome from the discovery report in MS1. The features will be fully functional but scoped to a level of detail reasonable for a reference implementation (as opposed to a mainnet-ready solution).

3) Dev activity log: A detailed log of the development activities that were required for the Substrate client customization. This log will serve as guidance for new developers wishing to understand the process with the goal of implementing their own versions.

Course 1 & 2 Curriculum as Outlined in Proposal*:

COURSE 1: HISTORY & EMERGENCE OF DECENTRALIZED FINANCE TOOLS

This course familiarizes the learner with decentralized finance concepts, structures, and use cases. Lessons include:

  1. Centralized Finance vs. Decentralized Finance
  2. Cardano DeFi vs. Other Blockchain Ecosystems
  3. Decentralized Applications
  4. Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs)
  5. Decentralized Exchanges
  6. Decentralized Lending & Borrowing
  7. Governance & Voting
  8. Platform Use Cases

COURSE 2: FUNDAMENTALS FOR PARTICIPATING IN CARDANO

This course provides a walkthrough of the process for getting involved in the Cardano ecosystem. Lessons include:

  1. Choosing & Setting Up a Cardano Wallet
  2. Securing Cardano Assets
  3. Staking & Stake Pools
  4. Testnet Faucets
  5. Cardano Decentralized Exchanges (DEX)
  6. Acquiring Cardano Native Tokens on a DEX
  7. Understanding Market Capitalization and Tokenomics
  8. Basics of Staking, Liquidity Providing (LP) & Yield Farming (Concepts)
  9. Decentralized OnChain Governance
  10. Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAO)
  11. Improvement Proposals, Voting Rounds, Voting Power
  12. Monitoring Your Positions
  13. Crypto Resources: CoinGecko, TradingView, TapTools, Defillama, and Others

*The team may re-arrange content or order, rename lesson titles, and make other relevant adjustments as necessary during production to create the ideal delivery of all the content promised in the proposal. This leaves room for Cardano ecosystem changes, new protocol offerings, and emergent learning.
title: Courses 1 & 2 Content Complete

Course 3 & 4 Curriculum as Outlined in Proposal*:

COURSE 3: DECENTRALIZED EXCHANGES (DEXes)

Decentralized Exchanges offer the opportunity for leveraging assets in diverse ways. There are two types of Cardano DEXes with different considerations, risks, and benefits.

  1. Automated Market Maker DEXes 
  2. Exploration of Risks: Impermanent Loss
  3. Exploration of Benefits: Multiple Yield Options
  4. Walkthrough Demonstration using Cardano AMM DEXes
  5. Different AMM DEX Participation Strategies in Action:
  6. Passive: Vault Staking (Low Risk)
  7. Active: Liquidity Providing (Medium Risk)
  8. Aggressive: Liquidity Bootstrapping Events, Zap Features & Arbitrage (High Risk)
  9. Order Book DEXes
  10. Exploration of Risks: Human Error & Learning Curve
  11. Exploration of Benefits: Multiple Yield Options
  12. Walkthrough Demonstration using Cardano Order Book DEXes
  13. Different Order Book DEX Participation Strategies in Action:
  14. Passive: Vault Staking (Low Risk)
  15. Active: Liquidity Providing (Medium Risk)
  16. Aggressive: Market Making & Arbitrage (High Risk)

COURSE 4: DECENTRALIZED LENDING & BORROWING

  1. How does Decentralized Lending & Borrowing work?
  2. Risks of Supplying/Lending Your Assets
  3. Benefits of Supplying/Lending Your Assets
  4. Risks of Borrowing Assets
  5. Benefits of Borrowing Assets
  6. Liquidation & Health Factor Considerations
  7. Market Participation Rewards
  8. Different Participation Strategies in Action:
  9. Passive: Supplying/Lending Only vs. Staking Only OR Both (Low Risk)
  10. Active: Borrowing Against Your Supplied Assets (Medium Risk)
  11. Aggressive: Debt Leveraging Strategies (High Risk)
  12. Understanding the Responsibility for Your Decisions & Actions

*The team may re-arrange content or order, rename lesson titles, and make other relevant adjustments as necessary during production to create the ideal delivery of all the content promised in the proposal. This leaves room for Cardano ecosystem changes, new protocol offerings, and emergent learning.

description:
Technical report with smart contract design and platform architecture

We will write a technical report discussing the overall platform architecture, including Web2’s backend (Python) and frontend (ReactJS) components, as well as the proposed on-chain approach. This report will outline use cases and requirements, along with functionality and objectives of smart contracts in the platform. The on-chain approach will focus on discussing operations that require immutability and decentralization. That is, registering contribution scoring (topic creation, evidence and content submission, voting on topic claims, reviewing claims, etc.), reward distribution (ensuring contributors are compensated based on verified contribution scores), governance mechanisms, among others.

Off-chain components will discuss how to handle resource-intensive tasks and dynamic operations. Fact-checking analysis, content processing including AI and human review workflows, will be conducted off-chain, with results fed into on-chain when appropriate. Data assets, media files, and detailed claim descriptions, will be stored on Web2 services (i.e., triplestores, databases, and storage services) with future plans for using decentralized storage solutions like IPFS or Arweave, with hashes stored on-chain for verification. Reputation management, user authentication, and anti-abuse mechanisms will also operate off-chain, updating on-chain data as necessary to reflect contributors' engagement and system integrity. 

The smart contract design in the report will focus on drafting the contract logic, as the following:

  • Programming language: Assessing which language would be better for integrating with backend (Aiken, Marlowe, opshin, Plutus, plu-ts)
  • Inputs: Define what data the contract will accept (e.g., user contributions, votes).
  • Outputs: Specify what the contract will produce (e.g., token distribution, verified scores).
  • Validation Rules: Write conditions for valid transactions (e.g., signatures, thresholds for rewards).
  • State Management: Use the EUTXO model to define how the contract’s state transitions with each transaction.
title: Platform Architecture and Smart Contract Design

description:
Provenance, or the verification of the origin and history of the content, is crucial for the d-FCT platform. In this milestone, we will implement smart contract (output 1) and backend features (output 2) to ensure the authenticity and traceability of contributions made by users. In the smart contract side, this involves creating components to log transactions with submission's history using blockchain immutability, tracking user inputs, votes, and evidence provided for each fact-checked item. This will use Cardano’s blockchain to ensure transparency and accountability across the verification process. The use cases and programming language used to implement the smart contract will be defined in the Milestone 1 technical report. The backend features include server-side endpoints and components for keeping necessary metadata described in the Milestone 1 technical report in a relational database (i.e. postgresql).

  1. smart contract for provenance
  2. backend features for provenance
title: Develop Provenance Mechanisms

description:
• Scope Document: A comprehensive outline detailing the project's goals, objectives, and deliverables.
  • User Stories: A set of narratives capturing the needs and wants of the end-users.
  • DApp Design - UML diagrams: Visuals depicting the DApp’s functional behaviour and structure.
  • Component Diagrams: Highlighting the organization and dependencies among components. For a DApp, this might include smart contracts, web frontends, backend servers, external APIs, oracles, etc.
  • Use Case Diagrams: These help in identifying the different actors (users, other systems, or DApps) and their interactions with the DApp. This can show how a user might initiate a transaction, query the blockchain, or interact with smart contracts.
  • State Machine Diagrams: Very relevant for smart contracts to depict the different states a contract can be in (e.g., open, closed, funded) and the transitions between these states, triggered by transactions or events.
  • Class Diagrams: Useful for representing the structure of the datums of smart contracts.
  • Sequence Diagrams: These can depict the interactions over time between users, the DApp, external systems, and the underlying blockchain. This might show the sequence of calls to a smart contract function, how events are emitted, or how off-chain components interact with the blockchain.

Key Legislators:


Legislators will primarily include current or elected members of national or supranational legislative bodies such as Members of Parliament, Senators, or Congress members. Priority will be given to those in active roles or officially juried positions within the legislative branch.

European Commission representatives will also be invited, as this body drafts proposed legislation that significantly influences EU member states. Additionally, members of the European Parliament with roles in relevant committees (e.g., digital assets, finance, or technology) are a key focus.

In jurisdictions where ministries play a legislative role, such as Ministries of Finance or equivalent bodies, we will extend invitations where relevant. This is particularly applicable to cases where these ministries shape policies directly affecting blockchain and digital assets. While we will prioritize individuals with active or elected roles, having a demonstrated interest in digital assets, Web3, or related topics is essential, though they do not necessarily need prior track records on the subject.


Key Regulators:


Regulators are not the primary focus of this event, as there are other forums dedicated to their needs. However, in specific cases where their presence is deemed relevant—such as representatives from financial authorities, central banks, or securities commissions who significantly influence blockchain policies—we will include them on a limited basis. 1. Core program modules delivered: Module outlines, workshop materials, attendance records, and feedback surveys. Target attendance and response rate of 80%.
  2. Cardano-specific modules delivered: Module outlines, workshop materials (including code samples or practical exercises), attendance records, and feedback surveys. Target attendance and response rate of 80%.
  3. Investor readiness workshops conducted: Workshop materials, attendance records, documentation of investor meetings, and feedback surveys. Target attendance and response rate of 80%.
  4. Workshops and mentoring sessions conducted: Schedule of sessions, attendance records, and feedback surveys. Target attendance and response rate of 80%.
  5. Startups connected with investors and mentors: List of connections, documentation of meetings, and feedback from startups. Target response rate of 80%.
  6. Mid-program progress reports collected: Standardized template, timely submission of reports, and a summary of key findings.


Note:

The number of sessions will be outlined in Milestone 1. Session recordings will not be available to the public because the intellectual property belongs to the speakers and facilitators. Additionally, mentoring sessions often involve confidential discussions between startups and mentors/investors, making recording impractical.

Response rate is the percentage of participants who attend a session, workshop, or meeting, calculated by dividing the number of attendees by the total number of founders in the program.

The number is arbitrary. While we aim for high participation, but recognize that early-stage, investment-ready founders have demanding schedules and occasional drop-offs are expected due to unforeseen events, meetings with clients, or potential investors during the program.

acceptance_criteria:
* Output 1.1: Script runs in a Nix environment, has adjustable parameters in a config file (number of guardians, decryption threshold, number of voters and their votes, etc), saves logfiles, and creates a set of valid election artifacts including a final decrypted tally.

* Output 1.2: Script runs in a Nix environment, reads a set of election artifacts, and either returns 0 (yes, the entire election is valid) or throws an error message saying which section/property failed to verify. Known good artifacts from the ElectionGuard project should verify. The artifacts generated by the script in Output 1.1 should verify. Good artifacts broken manually (for example by changing or removing a vote, or changing one of the final tallies) should fail to verify.

* Output 1.3: Script runs in a Nix environment, generates valid and not-quite-valid elections with a range of config parameters, confirms that the (valid) final tallies match the config files, and confirms that valid artifacts verify but not-quite-valid ones do not.
description:
* Output 1.1: Script that runs a single election locally in “God mode” (controlling everything, logging inputs + outputs) using Docker, Podman, Arion, or similar.

* Output 1.2: Script that verifies the election artifacts generated in Output 1.1 using one of the verifier reference implementations.

* Output 1.3: Script that generates arbitrary election configs, runs the elections, and verifies them.
title: ElectionGuard components: run and verify elections locally

acceptance_criteria:
* Output 2.1: One or more markdown docs (with figures where helpful), and one whiteboard-style video. The video should include enough detail that people already familiar with Cardano and EUTXO will feel they generally understand the design without reading the docs, but shouldn't go over ~10 minutes. The docs should be detailed enough that a programmer would be able to say what each file and smart contract operation does, but not be an exhaustive reference with all function parameters, schemas etc.


* Output 2.2 script:

  * Runs in a Nix environment

  * Deploys an election contract to one of the public testnets

  * Submits transactions updating the contract for each step in the election

  * Uploads matching file(s) to IPFS at each step

  * Does not need to be hooked up to electionguard yet; static files from a previous run are OK


 * Output 2.3 script:

   * runs in a Nix environment

   * takes the address of the election contract as a parameter

   * reads the election contract state

   * finds and downloads the matching files from IPFS

   * builds up a valid election record

   * verifies the final record using the verifier from output 1.2

   * can monitor state and fetch files incrementally while the election script from output 2.2 is running, or be run afterward
description:
* Output 2.1: Documentation of the design: smart contracts, on-chain data, off-chain data.

* Output 2.2: Script that build and uploads the on-chain + off-chain data for a single election.

* Output 2.3: Script that downloads and verifies the on-chain + off-chain data for a single election.
title: Blockchain-related components: smart contracts, on-chain data, IPFS

acceptance_criteria:
* 3.1 script:

 * Runs in a Nix environment

 * Has adjustable parameters in a config file (number of guardians, decryption threshold, number of voters and their votes, etc)

 * Saves logfiles

 * Deploys an election contract to one of the public Cardano testnets

 * Electionguard components ("roles") submit transactions updating the contract for each step in the election

 * Electionguard components upload matching files to IPFS at each step

 * Builds up and verifies a set of valid election artifacts as in script 2.3

 * Uses the public testnet + IPFS for all communications between ElectionGuard components, except:

   * The test script can pass each one the initial election contract info

   * Shared resources can be deduplicated for efficiency, for example only one cardano-node and one ipfs-cluster rather than one per component


* 3.2 script satisfies criteria from 3.1, plus these (copied from 1.3):

 * generates valid and not-quite-valid elections with a range of config parameters

 * confirms that the (valid) final tallies match the config files

 * confirms that valid artifacts verify but not-quite-valid ones do not


* 3.3 scripts:

 * Broken into at least 3 that can be run on different computers:

   * one for administering an election (admin + guardian roles)

   * one for voting (mediator + voter roles)

   * one for verification (similar to output 2.3)

 * All run in Nix environments

 * All have basic but human-readable command line interfaces

 * Out-of-band setup info is passed between computers via QR codes or by USB + text copy/paste

   * voting and verification machines need election contract info

   * admin needs mediator info to authorize it to vote

 * All other communication between computers happens over a public Cardano testnet + IPFS


* 3.4 meetup:

 * Should be at least myself + 2 other people in real life

 * If everyone agrees to it, I film parts of the event for the closeout video

 * I bring 3+ computers (one per script, not per person) set up to run the multi-computer scripts

 * I briefly explain the system, including the Benaloh challenge and which properties can be proven vs which ones are out of scope/externally managed (voter registration, for example)

 * I briefly explain what the demo does now and what I want to propose next (future funding rounds)

 * We try at least one round of coming up with questions to vote on, voting, and looking at the results

 * I ask people to fill out the surveys

 * Question & answer time

* 3.4 survey questions:

 * Would something like this realistically improve your confidence in an election vs how they're done now? (Rate on a scale)

 * Are there parts of the design that aren't clear to you, or you think might not be clear to other voters? (Long answer)

 * What do you think of the proposed next steps... Do they seem worth funding? (Rate on a scale) Anything you would add to or remove from the priorities?


* 3.5: Final closeout report is publicly available in the github repo (https://github.com/jefdaj/electionguard-cardano). Includes survey responses and a summary of lessons learned from them.


* 3.6: Final closeout video is publicly available, with link in the github repo.

  4. Get Current Era (this is an integer value representing the current era of the ledger)
  5. Get Current Tip of the Ledger (the slot number and header hash of the last block that has been processed by the ledger)
  6. Get current Block Height (the chain’s highest block number)
  7. Get Current Epoch number (the current epoch of the ledger)
description: A Github repository publicly available with an Elixir application, documentation on how to use the application to connect to a Cardano node and issue Ledger Queries and a Dockerfile. The Elixir application should be able to establish a connection to a fully synced Cardano Node and issue the following ledger state queries supported for the Conway era: Get current era, Get current tip, Get current block, Get current epoch.
title: Handshake and Ledger Queries

description:
Objective: Create a prototype demonstrating the transfer of native Cardano assets between two isolated Hydra Heads using atomic payment transactions.

Details: Atomic transactions ensure that either all operations across the two Hydra Heads succeed or none do, preventing partial failures and avoiding liquidity traps. This milestone will validate whether native assets like USDM or ADA can move seamlessly across separate L2 instances. Using the classical approach of Hashed Timelock Contracts (HTLCs) a baseline payments scenario is established for next milestones. This milestone also includes a first design of the equivalent ad-hoc ledger approach (only for payments) outlined in the paper to get a first grasp on complexity of the approach.

Deliverables:

  • Working code showcasing atomic asset + data transfers using HTLCs
  • Draft of smart contracts for ad-hoc eUTxO ledger transactions (on-chain code)
  • A technical report documenting the HTLC approach, how the ad-hoc ledger design works and any challenges encountered
title: Atomic transactions across two Hydra heads

acceptance_criteria:

  • Documented how generic smart contract transactions map onto ad-hoc ledgers (nominal case, no dispute resolution)
description:
Objective: Enable smart contract execution between distinct L2 ledgers, such as placing a bid on Midgard from a Hydra Head.

Details: This milestone explores cross-ledger calls where dApps on one L2 can interact with smart contracts on another. Example: a user on Hydra participates in an auction or lottery contract deployed on Midgard.

Deliverables:

  • A demo of smart contract interactions across L2s using ad-hoc ledgers.
  • A framework for structuring cross-ledger calls, including design patterns for request-response flows and transaction finality guarantees.
title: Design and demonstrate smart contract interactions using ad-hoc ledgers

acceptance_criteria:
• Payments can be executed across two two-party ledgers with a single inermediary using an ad-hoc multi-party ledger (single-hop).
  • Payments can be executed across two multi-party ledgers with multiple intermediaries (single-hop).
  • Payments can be executed across multiple L2 ledgers (multi-hop).
  • Assuming nominal operation of L2 ledgers (no dispute resolution), transactions either succeed in all ledgers or none.
  • Demonstrated scenarios on a public cardano testnet.
description:
Objective: Showcase payment transactions that flow through multiple L2 instances without breaking atomicity.

Details: Connected L2 ledgers can act as a payment aggregator where two or more L2s can settle transactions without requiring direct connections on dedicated state channels. This reduces the burden on users by minimizing the number of transfers they need to make between ledgers. This milestone is about single- and multi-step, atomic payments, ensuring that even if the payment involves several L2s, it either completes fully or reverts safely. Notably, this does not include any dynamic "routing" and purely static setups of Hydra heads and Midgard rollups, creating a blueprint for more complex multi-hop payment networks.

NOTE: This milestone deliberately combines the originally proposed milestones 4 and 5 from Ideascale, due to the great similarity between the central hub-and-spoke model (single-hop) and payments across multiple ledger (multi-hop) scenarios.

Deliverables:

  • A working prototype demonstrating atomic transfers across three or more L2s.
  • Documentation of various possible topologies and scenarios.
  • Report comparing the efficiency of this model against point-to-point transactions and HTLC-based systems.
  • Report highlighting performance metrics of payment scenarios, including latency and transaction costs, along with recommended optimizations.
title: Payments across multiple L2s using atomic transactions

2. The dispute mechanism outlined in this paper is implemented for hydra-only setups.
  3. Explored a generalized dispute mechanism that also applies to heterogenous use between Hydra and Midgard L2 (in writing, no implementation).
  4. Written documentation or recorded video explaining the dispute mechanism(s).
  5. Main adversarial scenarios are covered by a test suite.
description:
Objective: Develop a mechanism for dispute resolution to ensure the integrity and liveness of cross-ledger operations, especially under adversarial conditions.

Details: Previous milestones have been relying on non-adversarial behavior (the happy path). The system will need to handle cases where one L2 attempts to withhold or delay part of a cross-ledger interaction. Midgard’s fraud proofs and Hydra’s state commitments provide the foundation for this milestone. This step ensures that transactions remain live and disputes can be resolved in favor of honest participants.

While for the hydra-only scenario, this research paper outlines a dispute mechanism, this milestone also aims to conduct some research & development of a similar, generalized mechanism that can be used in heterogenous setups between Hydra and Midgard. Due to the early development stage of Midgard, there is quite some uncertainty on this part and we can only commit to have this explored in a design document and (likely) not implemented.

Deliverables:

  1. Implementation of a dispute mechanism ensuring that cross-ledger operations cannot get stuck indefinitely.
  2. Test scenarios involving adversarial actions to validate the solution.
title: Dispute resolution and eventual liveness in cross-ledger interactions

acceptance_criteria:
• Onboarding Barca Vision Community Members


We will target over 100K Barça fans through the Barça Discord server and expect between 1000 and 3000 unique users to participate in the program. Users will be onboarded into the program through dedicated channels on Discord and their evaluation will be done through the Andamio platform.  We expect an active participation between 50% and 80%; defining active participation as those users who complete the courses they register for.  That is, as we offer two courses in this cycle, we expect, approximately, to have an active participation between 1000 and 4800 users. The two limits that define active participation are given by:

  • Minimum active participation = 1000 unique users * 2 courses * 50% = 1000 users 
  • Maximum active participation = 3000 unique users * 2 courses * 80% = 4800 users


  • Learn-to-Work Cycles


Barça fans will complete a cycle by participating in two courses. Each course will consist of specific contents and assignments. Examples of assignments include: participate on Discord, attend an event, share an image, post a message on social media, solving a quiz, etc. Fans will obtain approval of the assignment submission (by the Barca Vision and Andamio teams according to the relevant domain being assessed) and then claim credentials.

Each course will have five assignments, the grading threshold will be: 

  • Less than three assignments not being performed correctly means failing the course.
  • Three assignments correctly performed allows passing the course.
  • Four assignments correctly performed will provide a merit qualification.
  • Five assignments correctly performed will provide a distinction qualification.

The quality of the content will be managed by Barca vision team and based on Barca vision standards. 


  • Discord: Engagement Activities


Under the Talent Lab space in Discord, we will have four dedicated channels, each described below, where we will do announcements at least twice a week.

  • Content exploration: forum style channel where the users can see a display of the courses
  • Student forum: the users can interact and engage with other learners
  • Student progress: where the students can check how far along they are in the course
  • Internships/experiences: where the students can explore new related job opportunities

We expect around 10000 interactions within the Discord dedicated channels within this cycle.


  1. Andamio platform: Evaluation and tracking


The web3 Andamio platform of Cardano’s ecosystem, connected to Discord, will host the evaluation of those courses completed by the fans. Andamio’s platform will allow users to be rewarded with NFTs/badges as they successfully complete the courses (see previous section). It will also allow, through a dashboard, for transparent and traceable auditing of the progress of all users per course and per cycle.

Taking into account the expected active participation, we anticipate the creation and delivery of between 1000 and 4800 NFTs/badges in this cycle. We will also track the following metrics through a dashboard: transactions, new wallets opened, Andamio Access Tokens minted (verified course completion, wallet-linked), and  NFTs and Ada distributed as rewards for completed Learn-to-Work cycles.

Onboarding Barca Vision Community Members

To onboard Barça community members, users will register with Barça ID and complete a short, interactive introductory course that familiarizes them with the platform and the Learn-to-Work program flow. 

As part of this process, we will showcase the documentary Masterpieces in the FC Barcelona Discord channel. This documentary highlights FC Barcelona’s first two NFT releases and explains the benefits of blockchain technology, serving as an entry point to the community’s digital ecosystem. 

https://one.fcbarcelona.com/en/videos/detail/221189

To encourage engagement, users who watch the documentary and successfully complete a quiz will be rewarded with an NFT. This NFT will act as a tokenized access pass, unlocking content from the Learn-to-Work program cycles while gamifying the onboarding experience.

Duration: 4-6 weeks per cycle.

• Sustainability with Plastiks - Past, Present and Future

Exploring FC Barcelona’s commitment to sustainability, this cycle will focus on the club’s collaboration with Plastiks. Barça’s first NFT collection with Plastiks was launched to fund plastic waste removal and support environmental efforts through digital collectibles. (More details: Plastiks Campaign)*This is subject to change based on milestone 1 content plan.

Community Engagement Activities


To foster participation and maintain momentum throughout the Learn-to-Work program, the following engagement initiatives will be implemented:


A dedicated Discord channel with weekly updates to keep the community informed and engaged.

• Progress highlights from the Learn-to-Work cycles

• Spotlights on top contributors and success stories

• Announcements about upcoming sessions, challenges, and rewards

• Engagement NFT as a Reward

Fans who actively participate and successfully complete a Learn-to-Work cycle will receive an Engagement NFT.

 This purpose-made digital asset will serve as an additional incentive, offering holders access to exclusive content, future opportunities, and potential perks within the Barça Vision ecosystem.

Objective:

Integrate the Private Distributed Cloud Service (PDCS) with the Partner’s infrastructure and conduct functional testing to validate system performance, stability, and operational readiness. This milestone also establishes the foundation for ongoing value tracking by implementing a usage metrics collection framework.


Outputs:

A. System Integration:

  • Verified System Integration Report: documentation of successful system integration with the partner’s IT environment (e.g., server nodes, data input/output, authentication layers). Signed confirmation from IT leads that integration is complete (names could be redacted).
  • Functional Testing Summary: Covers testing of core PDCS functions: file upload/download;  access controls; system responsiveness; fault tolerance scenarios. Documented with: test cases; pass/fail results; bug resolutions (if applicable)
  • Issue Tracking & Fix Report: tracks issues identified during integration/testing. The report is exportable from the internal system or documented in structured PDF.

B. Value Measurement Setup:

In parallel, define and document the disaster recovery (DR) strategy, ensuring enterprise-level resilience and business continuity preparedness.

acceptance_criteria:
given some text (the source code) the tokenizer can iter over it emitting the corresponding tokens

for example the text "const thing = 2;" will produce the tokens "const" "identifier" "thing" "equals" "literal integer" "2" "semicolon".
description:
a Tokenizer class taking as input the source text and with the necessary methods to emit the tokens of the language

this is the first step of the compiler, where from a raw piece of text we get something that is more easy to work with "tokens", wich are nothing more than smaller pieces of text that carry some meaning on their own (eg. words).

The output of this milestone is the implementation of this first part of the compiler
title: Tokenizer

acceptance_criteria:
given a source text it is possible to build the AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) representation of it.

The AST is just an in-memory representation of the source code. where the pieces of text are "grouped" based on known structures.

so at this point, the compiler is able to "see" these structures and store them in variables.
description:
a class that takes as input a Tokenizer from the previous milestone and consumes the emitted tokens to build an AST representation of the source language.

during construction of the AST, the parser makes sure that the syntax of the language is respected.

at this point the compiler starts making some sense of the source code

here syntatic errors are catched, for example "const thing = 2;" is valid syntax, but "const const = 2;" is not, because "const" is a keyword of the language and cannot be used for the name of a variable.
title: Parser

acceptance_criteria:
The IR (and UPLC as consequence) is built from a program

At this point the compiler is able to produce valid contracts that can be used on-chain
description:
From the AST we proceed to check the semantic of the program and compile it to a lower level intermediate representation (IR) used to further optimize the contract.


This steps includes:

  • Type checking
  • desugaring (for loops etc.)
  • rewriting expression in semantic equivalent
  • etc.


Here the compiler has the full picture of the program and is able to finally "translate" the source code to something closer to the language of the blockchain (uplc)
title: Compilation to IR

1. Completion and review of smart contract prototype: A functional mock contract that simulates token issuance, access control, and royalty logic. Reviewed and signed off by Iagon and Würth representatives. (Note: Final testing will occur on testnet in Milestone 4.)
  2. The automated royalty calculation and payout process is successfully implemented in code, tested, and validated against business rules. Both teams' Iagon & Wurth feedback must be documented and used to refine the logic. 
  3. Documentation of mock API calls is completed and reviewed by Iagon and Würth, showcasing endpoints simulating data exchange with DIS.
  4. The API specification document is reviewed and approved by Iagon and Würth. The version is shared with Catalyst reviewers, confirming the current state of endpoint design and integration logic across the project.
description:
Objective: 

Design initial smart contracts for secure IP tokenization, access control, and royalty distribution to ensure compliance with business rules. Implement off-chain API prototypes to interact with mock contracts.

Outputs:

  1. Smart Contract Prototype: Establish a functional mock smart contract simulating token issuance, access control logic, and royalty distribution. This mock contract will serve as the foundation for future testnet deployment and simulate key transaction logic outlined in the proposal.
  2. Royalty Mechanism: Implement and test the royalty logic in code (even in mock form), ensuring it automates payout calculations based on business rules. The royalty mechanism implemented in this milestone directly builds upon the design output from Milestone 1 by operationalizing the logic for calculating and distributing royalties that was previously conceptualized. It translates the tracked transaction types and royalty splits into executable payout rules.
  3. Off-chain API prototype: Demonstrate and document mock API calls that simulate real integration scenarios with Würth’s DIS (Digital Inventory Services). API endpoints will showcase basic data flow between front-end/backend and the contract logic.
  4. API Endpoint Specification Document: An internal document listing agreed API endpoints related to license execution, royalty distribution, and IP management, validated jointly by Iagon and Würth at this milestone. This reflects the current implementation and may evolve further in alignment with enterprise development practices.
title: Smart Contract Design and Initial Service Development

acceptance_criteria:

description:
Objective:

Develop APIs and UX to integrate the tokenization platform with Würth’s DIS (Digital Inventory Services), enabling seamless user interactions with 3D IP files. Additionally, design the Iagon storage connector for integration with the DIS. This milestone establishes the user-facing integration and sets the foundation for end-user interactions.


Outputs:

  1. API Documentation: Initial API specifications detailing endpoint structures, input/output parameters, and integration logic for DIS.
  2. Integration Test Results: Detailed test reports validating data exchange, performance, and system response between the platform and DIS.
  3. UX Designs: Wireframes or clickable prototypes showing end-to-end user flows for ordering and 3D printing interactions. These designs will be finalized and delivered regardless of implementation needs. If UI already present, screenshots may be provided instead.
  4. Storage Connector Design: Technical documentation describing the architecture and design plan for the Iagon storage connector with Würth’s DIS.

acceptance_criteria:
1. Mainnet Deployment: Smart contracts are deployed on Cardano mainnet with all core functionality enabled (IP tokenization, royalty distribution, and order processing). Integration testing logs and results confirm functional behavior. A detailed mainnet deployment report will be provided as a core deliverable, reviewed and approved by Wurth. Approval will be documented via signed feedback, meeting notes, or confirmation email (personal data may be redacted)﻿
  2. Partner Approval: DIS integration, print queue interaction, and all frontend/backend workflows are reviewed and approved by Würth representatives. Meeting summaries and approvals are documented.
  3. Smart Contract Audit Completed: Audit is conducted by an independent, qualified auditor. Findings are addressed prior to launch. The audit report is shared with Catalyst reviewers.
  4. Storage Connector Finalized: A production-level version of the Iagon storage connector is implemented. Evidence includes documentation and live demonstration or deployment walkthrough.
  5. Risk Mitigation Plan Delivered: A formal document summarizing risk identification, mitigation strategies, and architectural security decisions is submitted and aligns with Würth’s internal compliance governance. This document will be reviewed and approved by both Iagon and Wurth teams, shared with Catalyst reviewers as part of milestone completion.
description:
Objective:

Deploy the solution on mainnet and complete production readiness across all modules. This includes integration with Würth’s internal DIS and print queue, final validation of smart contracts (royalty distribution, IP tokenization, order processing), completion of the orchestrator and order apps, final deployment of the Iagon storage connector, and execution of a formal smart contract audit. This milestone represents the transition from prototype to enterprise-ready production deployment.


Outputs:

  1. Mainnet Deployment Report: A detailed report including evidence of live contract addresses, transaction hashes, logs, and documented tests for IP tokenization, order processing, and royalty distribution.
  2. Rollout Capability Confirmation: Iagon and Wurth sign-off on functionality includingDIS integration and print queue, confirming readiness for production use.
  3. Storage Connector Finalized: Production-ready version of the Iagon storage connector deployed or prepared for use within Würth’s Digital Inventory Service.
  4. Smart Contract Audit: Completion of an external smart contract audit by a qualified third-party security firm, covering all critical modules. Findings and remediations will be documented and shared.
  5. Solution Risk Mitigation Plan: A detailed internal risk analysis that outlines enterprise-grade mitigations and architectural decisions, completed in parallel to the audit to meet internal Würth compliance and governance processes.
title: Mainnet preparations and finalize implementation

acceptance_criteria:

  2. Performance Analytics: System metrics are actively tracked. A report summarizing transaction volumes, error rates, response times, and uptime is delivered with reviewer-facing outputs.
  3. Support System Activated: Ticketing system is fully functional. Additional support options are described in the final documentation.
  4. Reviewer Demo Materials Delivered: A full demo package is provided to Catalyst reviewers, including video walkthrough, logs, screenshots, and demo recordings.

description:
Objective:

Launch the platform on the Cardano mainnet for production use by Würth’s internal customers. Ensure stable performance through monitoring tools, and activate user support mechanisms. This milestone closes the project with full deployment, documentation, and transparency for community verification.


Outputs:

  1. Mainnet Launch Confirmation: Fully functional platform deployed for Würth-assigned users with all features operational (asset listing, license purchasing, royalty distribution, and print queue submission).
  2. Performance Monitoring Tools: Real-time analytics integrated to track metrics such as system uptime, smart contract transaction status, API response time, and storage access logs. Metrics finalized in coordination with Würth.
  3. User Support System: A dedicated ticketing system will serve as the primary support channel for internal Würth users. Additional support mechanisms — such as email-based workflows and system monitoring dashboards — will be implemented as needed based on operational requirements. The system architecture allows for modular support tools, ensuring adaptability without compromising transparency or user accessibility. Documentation will include current implementations at the time of delivery.
  4. Reviewer Transparency Package: To uphold transparency while respecting enterprise constraints, a complete non-interactive package will be delivered. This includes a high-resolution video walkthrough of user/admin flows, annotated screenshots of the production environment (with redactions as required by Würth’s compliance team), transaction logs, performance analytics, and API trace summaries. 
  5. Final Report & Close-Out Video: A comprehensive final report and video summarizing platform features, achievements, and future plans.
title: Deployment and Performance Optimization

acceptance_criteria:
Inspector Workflow: Inspectors can successfully log in, fill out, and submit inspection reports using the mobile application.

Internal Verification: The PT Inspeksi Mobil Jogja team can view, manage, and approve/reject submitted reports via the internal dashboard.

On-Chain Transaction: An approved report from the internal dashboard successfully triggers a transaction that immutably records the report's hash and key metadata on the Cardano testnet via the Blockfrost API.

Public Data Retrieval: The public-facing platform can successfully query the Cardano testnet (via Blockfrost) and accurately display the verified inspection history for a given vehicle.

Documentation & Security: All technical documentation is complete and publicly available in a GitHub repository and/or public Google Drive. The security audit report from Night Login Cyber Security Community is delivered, and any critical vulnerabilities identified have been addressed. Some may not be fixed yet.

Live Demonstration: A successful end-to-end video demonstration showcasing the entire data journey from inspection to public view is provided.
description:
Inspector Mobile Application (Flutter): A fully functional mobile application for PT Inspeksi Mobil Jogja's inspectors to conduct and submit digital reports from the field. This replaces their paper-based process. The application will be distributed through external download (all devices used by the inspectors are Android).

Internal Verification Dashboard (Web): A secure internal web dashboard for the PT Inspeksi Mobil Jogja team. This system allows for the review, management, and quality assurance of submitted inspection reports before they are committed to the blockchain.

Public Data Platform (Web): The public-facing website where end-users can search for and view the final, verified car inspection histories. This platform will feature a robust backend integrated with the Blockfrost API for on-chain data retrieval.

Blockfrost API Integration: Full integration with the Blockfrost API to anchor data (e.g., report hashes and metadata) onto the Cardano testnet. This approach replaces the initial plan for custom Plutus smart contracts, opting for a more mature, secure, and industry-standard method for this use case.

Comprehensive Documentation: Full technical documentation in Github and web docs for all developed components.

Third-Party Security Audit: A complete security review and penetration test of the entire integrated system, conducted by the Night Login Cyber Security Community. The output will be a formal report detailing findings and recommended remediations.
title: System Development, Integration, and Testing

  1. Transaction Construction and Serialization Coverage:
  2. 100% implementation of transaction types defined in Conway CDDL
  3. Automated test suite covering creation of all 5 types of transactions
  4. Test suite covering isomorphism of serialization/deserialization of at least 100 real mainnet transactions of different types (simple, with script execution, with governance). These tests should fail in Milestone 1.

  6. Quality Metrics:
  7. All public APIs documented with ScalaDoc
  8. CI pipeline enforcing compilation and tests passing across JVM and JS platforms

description:
Scala 3 Cardano Transaction Builder API and domain classes based on Conway CDDL definitions.

It's a Scala/Java API, not a REST API, so no TPS measurement can't be done. So here we provide a list of requirements for the API.

API expected to be similar to Lucid Evolution and Cardano Client Lib libraries to simplify adoption by users.

API should allow

  1. construct all types of transactions:
  2. spending, 
  3. minting, 
  4. using native and Plutus scripts, 
  5. staking, 
  6. governance
  7. serialize/deserialize transactions
  8. balance transactions
  9. calculate fees and script execution budgets

In Milestone 1 the API methods won't yet have platform specific implementations, so most functionality can not be functionally tested.

Instead, we'll prepare a set on unit tests that should fail in M1 but should pass after platform specific implementations after M2 for JVM (using Cardano Client Lib implementation) and M3 on JavaScript (using Lucid Evolution implementation).
title: Scalus TxBuilder API
