acceptance_criteria:
Formalize Marlowe Oracle Specification


  • Formal specification is written and includes:
  • Protocol overview and purpose
  • General description of system functionality
  • All data definitions, including message formats and data structures
  • All protocol states, including message sequences and flow control
  • Error handling, including exception management
  • Security considerations, including authorizations and encryption
  • Interface requirements, including API details and communication channels
  • Testing and validation procedures
  • Suggested metadata description for oracle datapoints.
  • Definitions of key terms
  • Appendices for optional details
  • Draft CIP successfully submitted and can be interacted with in the CF CIP repo
  • Stakeholder meetings with and questionnaire results from Oracle service providers are documented, with feedback collected and addressed via specification updates

Marlowe validator and runtime adaptations


  • All repos associated with these adaptations are OSS, with readme.md and appropriate OSS license (Apache 2.0 from the proposal)
  • Documentation for the format used in Marlowe datum for the Oracle choices, available in markdown in the repository. Documentation to include specifics sections as described in outputs section above.
  • Validator changes are fully documented and deployed in preprod environment
  • shows how Marlowe thread token handling approach has been simplified for data integrity
  • Runtime changes are fully documented and deployed in preprod environment
  • Includes clear descriptions of contract splitting and Merkleization of data
  • Clearly describes use case of establishing division points in contracts for contract developers
  • Existing integration tests passed will also be detailed.
description:
To formally define the Marlowe Oracle Protocol and ensure its acceptance and understanding within the Cardano community, a detailed Cardano Improvement Proposal (CIP) must be submitted. To fully support Oracle functionality, we need to adapt the existing Marlowe validator and runtime backend to handle Oracle data interactions efficiently and securely.

Formalize Marlowe Oracle Specification


  • Initial formal specification for Marlowe Oracle Protocol is documented and iterated via CIP submission and stakeholder feedback
  • Specification to include rationale and objectives for the protocol, technical requirements, functionality and integration points with and dependency on the existing Marlowe infrastructure.
  • Draft CIP proposal submitted to the Cardano Improvement Proposal repository
  • Details of the structure of the CIP are provided in the acceptance criteria below.
  • Feedback collected from Stakeholder engagement with Oracle service providers (e.g., Wolfram Blockchain Labs, Charlie3, Orcfax)
  • Feedback will be gathered through questionnaires and online meetings with representatives of Oracle service providers.

Marlowe Validator and Runtime Adaptations


  • Document the format used in Marlowe datum which can be accessed by other scripts to collect the Oracle choices.
  • This documentation will include the structure and schema of the datum, how it facilitates Oracle data collection, and examples of how it is used in scripts.
  • Simplify and document Marlowe thread token handling approach by the validator which facilitates safe Oracle data integration.
  • This will include a description of the current thread token handling approach, and the simplifications made, as well as describing how the schema ensures safe Oracle data integration.
  • Documentation and preprod deployment of runtime changes to allow Merkleization (code splitting technique) of contract code via directed contract code chunking  which  potentially  enables Oracle interaction.
  • Merkelization is a code splitting technique which enables large Marlowe contract execution in the resource limited on-chain environment..
  • The documentation will include a description of the technical changes made to the runtime, and of the benefits of these adaptations for Oracle interactions.

NOTE FOR REVIEWERS: the first two outputs here represent a simplification of the design that reflects work done on the system between proposal submission and acceptance. The original suggestions for these outputs are listed here for info:

  • Documentation and preprod deployment of validator changes to guard the Marlowe state output after contract finalization, facilitating Oracle data integrity
  • Documentation and preprod deployment of changes to allow Marlowe to output relevant contract state (choices) as a UTxO, facilitating Oracle data integration

Thanks for the feedback on our previous submission, we have taken onboard the notes and added additional information and clarification in our v2 submission below:

This milestone includes the following output:

  1. Developed and fully functional custom made web-application online demo including the following features, functionalities and data-layers:
  2. Automatically delineated field boundaries and planted area of 20,000 field boundaries firstly in Kenya 
  3. Super-high resolution Satellite data (RGB and pre-processed indices NDVI and EVI) served on the web-tile server (Mapbox) 
  4. NFT links; i.e. minting links embedded into each single individual field boundary enabling users and eco-systems to sample-mint a field boundary and associated unique digital identity for that particular field incl. payment link testing 
  5. Sample minted field boundaries in the demo link with associated properties


We have included the online demo as the milestone output as the primary development and workpackage involved in this phase is to develop the technology and integrate it into a digital solution, for enabling the value-chain (agriculture) to access and enrich the dataset, through creating unique digital identities for each agricultural field boundary and land border as well as farmer. 

The importance and significance of this milestone is to be the first data-set of digital, unique identifier for smallholder farmers in Kenya, i.e. this demographic has traditionally lacked access to data, agricultural technologies and sufficient lending and insurance services, the ability to decentralise this data and make it available not only to the farmer but also banks, insurance companies, agronomists, grain traders, crop input distributors and governments will enable farmers to decrease their operational costs and increase digitisation and optimisation.

  2. The second acceptance criteria will include the successful development of the core dataset integrated into the web-application, i.e. delineated field boundaries, super-resolved Sentinel-2 at 1 meter per pixel resolution (basemap with 3 dates from one growing season), historical (35+ years of vegetation data) from each unique growing (crop) season. 1. PByteString and PBitString support all of CIP-122 and CIP-123 operations safely and without builtin calls.
  2. CIP-121 conversion primitives work safely between PInteger, PByteString, and PBitString.
  3. Compilation and semantic tests validate these operations. 
  4. At least one type class generalization exists for PByteString and PBitString.
  5. Documentation is complete and explains usage, limitations, and invariants. Haddock documentation is published with new additional builtins.
description:
1. Extensions to the existing PByteString API to support CIP-122 and CIP-123 without unsafe builtin calls. This will be checked on the typelevel to ensure applications to builtin calls are always valid. 
  2. A new PBitString type with functions for CIP-122 and CIP-123 bit-oriented operations. 
  3. An API for CIP-121 conversion primitives involving PInteger, PByteString, and PBitString. Examples of new operations will be provided in the form of test cases. 
  4. Type class generalizations of the new operations with instances for PByteString and PBitString.
  5. Full test suite for compilation and semantic correctness for all functionalities, including property tests and compilation tests. The test suite will ensure said builtin functions we provide are correctly typed and have correct operation. We do not provide test cases for the operations themselves as they are already thoroughly tested by the plutus-core library. 
  6. API-level documentation and tutorials for all new types and functions. Haddock documentation will be auto-generated on each release and be published on the github pages.
title: Plutarch bitwise support

acceptance_criteria:
1. Behavior of pcontains is correct and is verifiable by regression tests and property tests.
  2. A type class for predecessor functionality, as well as laws describing the meaning of this functionality, exists.
  3. A type class for successor functionality, as well as laws describing the meaning of this functionality, exists.
  4. PPosixTime is a lawful instance of the type classes from 2 and 3.
  5. Negative PPosixTime is supported correctly with unit and property test cases. 
  6. plutarch-extra integrated, and plutarch-orphanage exists as a separate library.
  7. NoTracing removes all tracing code from Plutarch scripts. Golden files for scripts compiled with and without NoTracing are provided to demonstrate correct behavior of NoTracing option.
description:
1. Separate type classes for abstracting the predecessor and successor operation, with laws to ensure that these behave appropriately. PPosixTime must be a lawful instance of both of these.
  2. Support for negative PPosixTime values.
  3. Bugs regarding pcontains(issue #705). 
  4. Utility functions from plutarch-extra integrated into Plutarch which will reduce complexity of repository and setup. Required functions and utility types will be moved into the plutarch library itself.
  5. plutarch-orphanage separated into its own library. All the orphan instances, mainly instances for QuickCheck testing library, will be isolated into a single package for better code practice and easier upstreaming in the future.
  6. NoTracing option ensures elimination of all tracing code. By removing all traces, scripts can be further minimized without any script resources taken up by trace messages and pshow functions.
  7. Tests validating these enhancements.
title: Plutarch Core Enhancements

acceptance_criteria:
• SOP encoding is integrated into Plutarch, with basic operations similar to PData. Test cases must be provided as a demonstration.
  • Multi-representation types (Scott, Data, SOP) are fully supported, and conversions between them work seamlessly, demonstrated by a test suite.
  • The PAsData infrastructure is reworked with the new multi-representation system to be more ergonomic and efficient for end users. Examples will be provided to demonstrate the changed interface.
description:
• Add SOP encoding to Plutarch, alongside Scott and Data encodings, and provide low-level operations for SOP encoding. UPLC version 1.1.0 introduced additional terms to encode Sum-of-Product at the UPLC term level. Since deconstruction of SOP terms can be done in one step, it yields better performance when compared to Scott and Data encoding.
  • Enable multi-representation types (Scott, Data, SOP). The data representation system in the internal will be reworked to have more flexibility and approachable when supporting three representations–Scott, Data, SOP–at the same time.
  • Tests to ensure that all three encodings (Scott, Data, SOP) work properly and that conversions between them are correct. Unit test cases and property based round-trip test cases will be provided to ensure decoding and encoding of each representation is behaving correctly.
title: Plutarch: SOP Encoding and Multi-Representation Support

acceptance_criteria:
1. Optimization utilities for recursion unrolling and size optimization are functional, and their improvements are visible by numerical records generated by golden for regression test and performance benchmark .
  2. Additional optimizations based on SOP support and multi-representation are implemented and effective, and, again, their improvements are visible by numerical records generated by golden and benchmark.
  3. Additional features also provided test cases covering each use case for added features.
  4. The UPLC-benchmark repository is a Fund10 project ( https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/uplc-benchmark/introduction.html ) aimed at benchmarking Plutarch and other common languages. It relies on the common Cardano use cases of an NFT Marketplace and a Constant Product DEX. We will update these examples to use new features introduced in the latest release of Plutarch to show and quantify improvements for the community. Sample integration is provided via updates in UPLC-benchmark where each dApp projects can use as reference for their integration and this will be our integration roadmap.
description:
1. Provide utilities for unrolling recursion and size optimization in Plutarch, using compile-time transformations that generate each step of recursion in order to reduce “start-up” costs relating to general recursion using fixed point combinator.
  2. Implement additional optimizations based on SOP support and representation conversion. This includes, but not limited to, application optimization using the `Case` term of UPLC.
  3. Ensure all functionalities for SOP support, conversions, and optimizations are thoroughly tested and documented. Golden test suites and benchmarks demonstrate improvements on execution units and script sizes.
  4. Include detailed comparisons of script sizes and execution costs before and after optimization to quantify the improvements.
  5. Update documentation website to provide examples and guides on the new features added.
title: Plutarch Optimization of Utilities and Further Testing

  2. Boehm-Berrarducci encodings are being used for compatibility with the Milestone 1 type system. 
  3. Base functors are supported. 
  4. Encodings for data types (both SOP and Data) can be specified. Furthermore, different strategies for Data encodings have been implemented.
  5. All compound data types required by the V3 Plutus ledger API exist in the Milestone 1 library.
  6. Tests for Criterion 1 and 2 functionality exist and pass, for both the Plutus primitive operations and ledger data types.
  7. Haddocks exist documenting all extensions to the Milestone 1 library done in this Milestone.
  8. The CI from Milestone 1 has been extended to run the new tests added in this Milestone.
  9. The extended library has been published on Hackage as an update.
description:
1. We will implement a way of defining compound types in the Milestone 1 library.
  2. This implementation will use Boehm-Berrarducci encodings to be compatible with the Milestone 1 type system.
  3. We will add support for base functors to enable later work on elimination forms together with Turner totality.
  4. Specification of encodings (SOP and Data) for compound data types as part of their definitions will be included. There will also be a selection of different strategies for Data encodings.
  5. We will implement all the compound data types required by the Plutus ledger, specifically its V3.
  6. We will add tests to ensure that the type system from Milestone 1 behaves correctly on all Plutus primitive operations and on the ledger data types.
  7. These extensions to the Milestone 1 library will be documented as Haddocks.
  8. The CI from Milestone 1 will be extended to run the tests specified in point 3.
  9. We will publish the extended library on Hackage as an update.
title: Data type support

acceptance_criteria:
1. Milestone 1 and 2 library has gained introduction and elimination forms in the ASG.
  2. A recursion scheme elimination form exists and uses catamorphisms.
  3. Base functors for existing compound recursive types, as well as Integer and ByteString exist.
  4. Tests using ASG construction have been added for the functionality of this Milestone, and pass.
  5. Haddock documentation exists for the public-facing new functionality added in this Milestone.
  6. The CI from Milestones 1 and 2 runs the new tests added in this Milestone successfully.
  7. The extended library has been published on Hackage as an update.
description:
1. We will extend the Milestone 1 and 2 library to support both introducing (creating) and eliminating (pattern matching and folding) values in the Covenant ASG.
  2. Folding will use recursion schemes, specifically catamorphisms.
  3. Base functors for existing compound recursive types, as well as Integer and ByteString Plutus core types, will be included.
  4. We will add tests to ensure that these forms behave correctly, by way of ASG construction (that is, 'end-to-end').
  5. We will document these extensions as Haddocks.
  6. The CI from Milestones 1 and 2 will be extended to run the tests specified in point 2.
  7. We will publish the extended library on Hackage as an update.
title: Introduction and elimination forms

acceptance_criteria:
1. At least two conformance cases of the serial form exist.
  2. All conformance cases deserialize correctly and without error
  3. An implementation in Haskell of serialization and deserialization of Covenant exists, as an extension to the library in Milestones 1 through 3.
  4. The CI for the library in Milestones 1 through 3 runs the conformance cases to ensure they continue to pass.
  5. Haddock comments for new public-facing functionality from this Milestone exist.
description:
1. We will provide a specification of the JSON-based textual form of Covenant, as well as an implementation of that specification into the library from Milestones 1 through 3.
  2. We will provide at least two conformance cases, designed for use in tests for the implementation of the specification.
  3. These tests will be provided as part of the library from Milestones 1 through 3 as well.
  4. New public-facing functionality will have Haddock comments in the code.
title: Serial form

acceptance_criteria:
1. An executable for generating UPLC from Covenant's serial form exists. Due to its dependence on Plutus, this can be in a separate repository from the rest of Covenant.
  2. The executable accepts a path to a Covenant serial form.
  3. The executable, when given a valid Covenant serial form, emits valid UPLC, whose execution semantics match those intended by the Covenant serial form.
  4. The executable, when given an invalid Covenant serial form, does not perform a translation. Instead, it errors with a clear and appropriate message.
  5. All the Milestone 4 conformance cases translate correctly using the executable from Criterion 1.
  6. The c2uplc CLI will exist, and will have help text as instructions, available under a dedicated flag.
  7. Final closeout report is publicly available
  8. Final closeout video is publicly available
description:

  4. Final close-out report
  5. Final closeout video
title: c2uplc

acceptance_criteria:
1. All Plutus V3 types are implemented correctly and LambdaBuffers now supports codegen for all the supported language modules for these types
  2. All Plutus V3 types are covered by the golden tests ensuring execution outputs are as intended
  3. All Plutus V3 have roundtrip tests for Eq, Json and PlutusData type classes (where applicable) to ensure no data is corrupted or lost.  Integrate testing in CI/CD to ensure continuous testing when the source code changes and documentation clearly explains the updates.
  4. The output is suitable for Plutus V3 Types such as Voter, Delegatee and GovernanceActionID etc.  
  5. Documentation will cover new type support across Lambda buffer supported languages and will appear on https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/lambda-buffers/ in the Catalyst Milestone F13 reporting.
description:
(Note :: we'd like to reorganize the order of milestones relative to the IdeaScale proposal while nevertheless committing to the same deliverables. In particular, this proposal is amenable to such a reorganization because each milestone touches an individual project, and there is nothing that linearly builds upon itself. We are doing so, with the Plomin fork incoming as of writing, because this will allow the quickest delivery of the most impactful projects to the Cardano community so that the value of this proposal is maximized.)

Implementation in repository:

  1. Implementing codegen for all modules (Haskell, Plutarch, PlutusTx, Rust, TypeScript, PureScript) for all the new Plutus Ledger types https://github.com/IntersectMBO/plutus/tree/master/plutus-ledger-api/src/PlutusLedgerApi/V3. This includes the new governance-related types, delegation types, and updated transaction types.
  2. Create new golden tests for the above types, for all language modules. For instance, we will have a set of files consisting of known-good JSON-serialized instances, and our testsuite will check that our implementation outputs these serialized values upon execution as expected. Although an exhaustive list of tests is not possible here, there are many Plutus types updated or new in V3 our library will support such as Vote, Voter, TxOutRef, TxInInfo, TxCert, etc and various concrete instantiations of each type to test - e.g., a VoteNo Vote, a VoteYes Vote, and so on.
  3. Create new roundtrip tests for Eq, Json and PlutusData type classes (where applicable) that will verify our type class instances serialise and deserialize without corruption, loss of information, etc by converting values to JSON and back, PlutusData and back, and verifying equality withstands.
  4. Implement new Plutus V3 types like Voter, Delegatee, GovernanceActionId, etc in plutus-ledger-api-rust and plutus-ledger-api-typescript
  5. Documentation explaining the updates accomplished towards LambdaBuffers Conway support
title: LambdaBuffers Conway support

acceptance_criteria:
• At least 1 pool UTxO is successfully created on the testnet script address, with correct parameters such as token pair, initial reserves, swap fees, and staking configuration stored in the UTxO datum.
  • At least 1 swap per direction is executed by spending the pool UTxO, updating the pool UTxO’s reserves as expected and providing accurate output UTxOs based on the AMM formula.
  • At least 1 liquidity addition and 1 liquidity removal are performed by spending the pool UTxO, with the pool UTxO updated accurately and LP tokens correctly calculated.
  • The pool script address depends on the staking key.
  • All interactions are verified on-chain, confirming correct updates to pool state and adherence to the staking configuration.
description:
• The smart contract will manage all interactions (pool creation, swapping, and liquidity management) using a single script address.
  • Pool creation involves creating a UTxO at the script address that represents the specific liquidity pool. The UTxO will store pool parameters in the UTxO datum, such as token pair, initial reserves, and a fixed staking configuration.
  • The contract will validate and execute swaps by spending the pool UTxO, ensuring accurate token exchanges and maintaining the pool’s state.
  • Liquidity providers can add or remove liquidity by interacting with the pool UTxO, and the contract will calculate and distribute LP tokens accordingly.
  • When creating a pool, the staking key will be embedded in the pool’s script address. This staking configuration will remain fixed for the lifetime of the pool, validated by the smart contract.
  • ADA in the pool will earn staking rewards, which is distributed proportionally to liquidity providers.
  • Smart contracts deployed and tested on Cardano testnet.
title: Smart Contracts Development

  • Liquidity management interactions include adding and removing liquidity, the amounts correctly calculated based on the AMM formula and a transaction is submitted to the blockchain.

description:

  • Basic swapping functionality includes querying pool states, calculating swap amounts based on the AMM formula, and submitting transactions to the blockchain.
  • The system should handle up to 20 testnet users, ensuring response times under 2 seconds for database queries and UI interactions.
  • A functional testnet version of the platform with the described features will be deployed.

  2. A publicly accessible community forum or chat server must be launched, tested by a small group of initial members or moderators for usability. Visibility is essential, so the forum or chat server must be linked or referenced across official documentation and repositories, reinforcing it as the primary hub for OADA community interaction.
  3. Ticketing System in place for support cases to be further escalated and formalized
  4. Guidelines for community participation and support.
  5. Community guidelines will be publicly posted, ensuring that newcomers understand the code of conduct, support protocols, and collaboration norms.
  6. Ticketing System in Place and Supported on Optim Discord
  7. Optim Finance Ticket system has been in place for years. While it is not possible to create a separate and parallel ticketing system for a particular use case, the Optim Team will show evidence that they are "Supporting all open tickets". This means timely responses by the team to open tickets. This gives an indication and reasonable basis to believe Optim team will continue supporting tickets related to developers looking to deploy OADA Open Front End.


**Note for Catalyst Reviewers - The Acceptance Criteria exactly maps to what the community voted on and passed in the proposal for this Milestone. Please review the language in the original proposal to see this is what was committed to and voted on. It is objectively a 1:1 representation. At the time of submission the 10,000 ADA for this Milestone was about $3,000 - much of which is allocated to necessary hours for developers and non-technical staff to service these channels.

Again, this Milestone states "Set up forums, chat groups, or other communication channels to facilitate community engagement, support, and collaboration." The team can only set up these channels and offer ongoing support when the need arises. It is not in the team's power to force participation by developers and others within a given time frame. Therefore it is not possible and not within the scope of this Milestone to prove we are actively supporting people for the OADA Open Front End implementation. It is possible people immediately require support, but it is also possible no one does.**

acceptance_criteria:
A. Technical Deliverables

1.1 Complete Technical Documentation

• Content Requirements: Must include integration approaches, potential risks, mitigation strategies, and a list technical terms. This document has to be signed by the CTO.

• Acceptance Test: CTO and outsourced developer lead must confirm that the documentation provides sufficient detail to begin implementation without additional clarification.

1.2 Requirements Analysis Document

• Content Requirements: Must list all functional and technical requirements, including use cases, user stories, and system dependencies which must be signed off by CTO. 

• Acceptance Test: All requirements must be traceable to project objectives and validated by the QA team and signed off by the CTO. 

1.3 Infrastructure Design Blueprint

• Content Requirements: Must include system architecture diagrams, component interactions, scalability plans, and security protocols and signed off by the CTO. 

• Acceptance Test: The architecture must pass a security and scalability review by the DevOps team and a test report must be approved by the CTO. 

1.4 Hardware and Software Procurement List

• Content Requirements: Must include itemized hardware and software specifications, quantities, vendors, and cost estimates which must be on a document approved by the COO and CTO.

• Acceptance Test: All items on the list must be verified as available and compatible with the infrastructure design and reflected in a document approved by the CTO. 

1.5 Overview Document

• Content Requirements: Must summarize project scope, technical approach, legal considerations, and intellectual property (IP) details approved by the COO and CTO. 

• Acceptance Test: COO must confirm that any IP and compliance considerations have been addressed.

1.6 Technical Specification Document

• Content Requirements: Must outline technical requirements, including APIs, data models, and system interfaces reflected in a Document signed off by the CTO. 

• Acceptance Test: Developers must confirm that the specifications are actionable and align with project goals and a report must be made and signed by the CTO.

1.7 Deployment Guide

• Content Requirements: Must include step-by-step instructions for setting up Cardano nodes, smart contracts, APIs, and testing procedures. Must be approved by Cardano development team and CTO. 

• Acceptance Test: Deployment team must successfully execute a test deployment using the guide.

1.8 Risk Assessment and Mitigation Plan

• Content Requirements: Must identify risks, their impact, likelihood, and mitigation strategies, rissks will be noted into a docuement and signed by the CTO

• Acceptance Test: Risk mitigation strategies must be validated through a simulated risk scenario.

B. Marketing & Branding Deliverables

2.1 Target Audience Profile Document

• Content Requirements: Must include demographic data, psychographic analysis, buyer personas, and market research findings, approved by the marketing director and CEO

• Acceptance Test: Marketing manager and CEO must confirm that the profiles align with campaign objectives.

2.2 Brand Audit Report, Strategy, and Pipeline

• Content Requirements: Must include current brand positioning, competitive analysis, strategy recommendations, and a pipeline for onboarding new brands.

• Acceptance Test: Strategy must be validated through onboarding of 1 brand with a successful sustainability dashboard.

2.3 Marketing Campaign Structure Document

• Content Requirements: Must outline campaign objectives, target audience, channels, budget, timelines, and KPIs. 

• Acceptance Test: Campaign structure must be ready for deployment.


2.4 PR Timeline Document

• Content Requirements: Must include a detailed schedule of PR activities, key milestones, and responsible parties.

• Acceptance Test: PR team must confirm that the timeline is feasible and aligns with campaign goals.

Additional Missing Criteria 

2.5 Initial Discussions with Minimum 3 Target Brands

• Content Requirements: Must include email confirmation from brands (3) accepting to move sustainability dashboard and plastic credit data from Celo blockchain to Cardano blockchain.

• Acceptance Test: Emails clearly indicate the approval move sustainability dashboard to Cardano.

2.6 Approved Marketing Campaign Structure for Brand Announcements

• Content Requirements: Must include campaign objectives, messaging, channels, and approval sign-offs.

• Acceptance Test: Campaign must be ready for deployment.

acceptance_criteria:
A. Technology 


1.1 Documentation Outlining How to Migrate Smart Contracts to Cardano 


Content Requirements: The documentation must include detailed steps, code examples, and best practices for migrating smart contracts to Cardano. 


Acceptance Test: Any developer must be able to successfully migrate a sample smart contract to Cardano using the documentation without requiring additional support. CTO will test this function and create a report confirming that it is complete and sign this document.  


1.2 Migration and Update of Current Smart Contracts (EVM Compatible) to Cardano 


1.2.1 Plastic Credits Smart Contracts 


Content Requirements: Smart contracts must be deployed on Cardano testnet and mainnet, representing real plastic recovery data (e.g., invoice, proof of payment, waste delivery documentation). 


Acceptance Test: The contracts must accurately tokenize plastic recovery data and pass functional testing. 


1.2.2 CO2 Credits Smart Contracts 


Content Requirements: Smart contracts must be deployed on Cardano testnet and mainnet, ensuring CO2 reductions are accurately tokenized. 


Acceptance Test: The contracts must accurately tokenize CO2 reduction data and pass functional testing. 


1.2.3 Smart Contracts Functional and Security Audits 


Content Requirements: Smart contracts must undergo functional and security audits, with results documented. 


Acceptance Test: The contracts must pass all audit tests without critical issues. 


1.3 Deploy Plastic and CO2 Credits Smart Contracts

Content Requirements:

Plastic and CO2 credit smart contracts must be deployed on both the testnet and mainnet. The contracts must be fully functional and capable of interacting with the marketplace. Deployment results must be documented. 

Acceptance Test:

The smart contracts must be successfully deployed on both networks and demonstrate seamless interaction with the marketplace without functional errors or critical issues.



1.4 NFT Redesign to Include Additional Data Points 


Content Requirements: NFTs must include geolocation of collection sites, point of origin and destination of waste, and this data must be visible in the NFT metadata and UI. 


Acceptance Test: Users must be able to retrieve and view the additional data points through the UI. 


1.5 Redesign the “Create Plastic Credit” Screen for Credit Issuers 


Content Requirements: The redesigned screen must be implemented and functional in the live environment, with improved usability and features. 


Acceptance Test: Credit issuers must confirm that the redesigned screen is functional and meets their needs. 


1.6 Deployment Plan Document 


Content Requirements: The document must include milestones, timelines, and a step-by-step technical process for deploying smart contracts. 


Acceptance Test: The deployment process must be validated through a pilot deployment. 


1.7 Deployment Checklist 


Content Requirements: The checklist must ensure smart contracts are correctly configured, system components are fully tested, and compliance with security best practices is met. 


Acceptance Test: The deployment must pass all checklist items without issues. 


 


B. Testing 


2.1 Infrastructure Testing 


Content Requirements: Testing must validate that cloud, Web3, and storage providers are correctly configured, and monitoring tools capture relevant system performance metrics. 


Acceptance Test: The infrastructure must meet all performance and configuration requirements. 


2.2 Migration and Functionality Testing for Cardano Smart Contracts 


Content Requirements: Smart contracts must execute correctly on Cardano testnet and mainnet, and transactions must be processed within expected timeframes. 


Acceptance Test: The contracts must pass all functional tests and meet transaction processing benchmarks. 


2.3 Plastic and CO2 Credits Transfer Test 


Content Requirements: Testing must verify that credits can be issued, transferred, and received without errors, and transactions must be reflected on the blockchain. Test cases must include edge scenarios (e.g., failed transactions, high network congestion). 


Acceptance Test: The credit transfer process can be considered acceptable when one credit (NFT) is transferred from one dashboard to another. 


 


C. Sales 


3.1 Complete Brand Onboarding Package 


Content Requirements: The package must include a step-by-step onboarding guide, clear definitions of onboarding requirements and expected outcomes, and a documented support process for brands. 


Acceptance Test: Brands must confirm that the onboarding process is clear and actionable. 


 


D. Marketing 


4.1 Marketing Materials for Brand Outreach 


Content Requirements: The materials must include a social media content strategy, outreach templates for businesses, and publicly available technical documentation for the developer community. 


Acceptance Test: The materials must be used successfully in outreach campaigns and result in measurable engagement.

• Acceptance Test: Developers must confirm that the diagram accurately represents the system and can be used to guide implementation.

• Content Requirements: The guide must provide detailed instructions, code samples, and troubleshooting tips for integrating the API and SDK. Must be approved by CTO 

• Acceptance Test: Developers must successfully integrate the API and SDK using the guide without requiring additional support. 

1.3 Security Implementation Plan 

• Content Requirements: The plan must detail security measures, protocols, and compliance requirements for the platform. Must be approved by CTO 

• Acceptance Test: The platform must pass a security audit based on the measures outlined in the plan. 

1.4 Cardano Wallet Connection 

• Content Requirements: The feature must allow users to connect their Cardano wallets seamlessly to the app. 

• Acceptance Test: Users must successfully connect their Cardano wallets and perform transactions without errors. 

1.5 + 1.5.1 Backend System Operability with Cardano Smart Contracts 

• Content Requirements: The backend must be fully integrated with Cardano smart contracts, ensuring seamless operability. 

• Acceptance Test: The backend must successfully interact with Cardano smart contracts in a test environment. 


1.6 Creation and Storage of Plastic and CO2 Credits (NFTs) 

• Content Requirements: Recovery entities and Brands must be able to create and store Plastic and CO2 credits (NFTs) within selected collections/roadmaps. 

• Users must be able to purchase plastic credits from a brand.

• Acceptance Test: A Recovery entity must successfully create and store NFTs, with proper tracking and storage confirmed. 

• A Brand must successfully create and store NFTs.

• A user must be able to pruchase an NFT.

• A user can purchase a plastic credit from a Brand and display it on their dashboard. 

1.7 Issuance and Linking of Plastic and CO2 Credits (NFTs) to Roadmaps 

• Content Requirements: At least three recovery entities must issue Plastic Credits (NFTs) and link them to predefined roadmaps for sale. 

• Acceptance Test: The NFTs must be successfully issued, linked to roadmaps, and available for sale in the platform. 

1.8 Testing and Results 

• Content Requirements: The testing process must be completed, and results must be documented, including test cases, outcomes, and any issues resolved. 

• Acceptance Test: The system must pass all defined test cases, with results confirming functionality and stability. 

 

B. Marketing 

2.1 Platform Demo Video 

• Content Requirements: Videos must demonstrate how to create a profile, edit it, and create Plastic/CO2 credits. Videos must be clear, concise, and uploaded to YouTube. Must be approved by marketing manager and head of product. 

• Acceptance Test: Users must be able to follow the video instructions to perform the demonstrated actions without errors. 


2.2 Brand-Specific NFT Campaign Templates

Content Requirements:


The template must be a dashboard that is operational and can serve as a placeholder for different brands and visually aligned with their branding guidelines.


Acceptance Test:

The marketing manager must confirm that the templates are easy to use, visually appealing, and effectively communicate their sustainability efforts.

acceptance_criteria:
A. Technology 

1. Automated Testing Scripts Documentation 

• Content Requirements: Documentation must include the results of automated testing scripts, performance metrics, and any identified issues. 

• Acceptance Test: The testing scripts must successfully monitor performance, and results must align with predefined benchmarks. 

2. Scalability Assessment Report 

• Content Requirements: The report must include scalability benchmarks, identified bottlenecks, and recommendations for improvement. 

• Acceptance Test: The platform must meet or exceed scalability benchmarks in a simulated high-load environment as defined and approved by the CTO.  

3. Extra Monitoring and System Alerts 

• Content Requirements: The monitoring system must include a control panel with visible, easy-to-understand alerts and performance metrics. 

• Acceptance Test: Alerts must trigger correctly during simulated system events, and the control panel must be usable by non-technical staff. 

4. Advanced Platform Features Document 

• Content Requirements: The document must clearly describe validated existing features and identify new features, including their functionality and benefits. 

• Acceptance Test: Developers must confirm that the document accurately reflects the platform’s features and guides implementation. 

5. Customer Feedback Documents 

• Content Requirements: The documents must include sample UX designs, customer feedback summaries, and proposed new features. 

• Acceptance Test: Users must validate that the proposed features address their feedback and improve their experience. 

6. Implementation Plan 

• Content Requirements: The plan must include a detailed timeline, development hour estimates, and resource allocation. 

• Acceptance Test: The plan must be validated through a pilot implementation phase. 

 

B. Marketing 

2.1 Expanded Brand Use Cases Document 

• Content Requirements: The document must explain how 2 new major brands will use the platform for ESG reporting and other purposes beyond anti-greenwashing. 

• Acceptance Test: The 2 brands must confirm that the use cases align with their needs and expectations. 

• Additional Requirement: Clarify that "onboarding" refers to the process of integrating brands into the platform and training them to use its features. 

2.2 New Campaign/Messaging Document 

• Content Requirements: The document must showcase the platform’s expanded features, highlight improvements over the previous version, and be suitable for industry and community events. 

• Acceptance Test: The document must be used to deploy a campaign in at least one industry or community event. 

 

Additional Missing Criteria  

2.3 Minimum 2 New Brands Actively Using Platform 

• Content Requirements: Evidence must show that 2 new brands are actively using the platform, including their profiles and activity logs. 

• Acceptance Test: Dashboard data must confirm the brands’ activity and engagement on the platform which can be measured by at least 1000 kilograms of plastic credits and at least 100 likes on the brand profile on the sustainability dashboard.  

2.4 Successful Scaling of Platform Infrastructure 

• Content Requirements: The scaling process must be documented, including benchmarks, load testing results, and performance improvements. 

• Acceptance Test: The platform must handle increased user loads without performance degradation as per benchmark to be set and approved by the CTO.  

2.5 Documented Brand Success Stories 

• Content Requirements: Success stories must include detailed metrics, testimonials, and case studies from brands using the platform. 

• Acceptance Test: The success stories must be published on Plastiks.io blog. 

2.6 Media Coverage in Major Publications 

• Content Requirements: Evidence must include links to articles, press releases, or mentions in major publications. 

• Acceptance Test: The coverage must result in at least one article, one press release and one major publication. 

2.7 Improved Platform Automation and Efficiency 

• Content Requirements: The improvements must be documented, including automation workflows, efficiency metrics, and implementation details. 

• Acceptance Test: The platform must demonstrate measurable efficiency gains in a test environment as determined and approved by the CTO

o The video and report must summarize the project’s progress, achievements, and documented environmental impact metrics from 2025.

o Video will be uploaded to Plastiks Youtube and the repport will be publised to Plastiks.io blog.

• Content Requirements:

o Evidence must show that 350,000+ plastic credits have been transacted on the platform.

• Acceptance Test:

o The platform and blockchain must reflect the transaction count in its reporting dashboard.

3. 10,000 Monthly Plastic Credit Transactions by Q4 2025

• Content Requirements:

o Evidence must show that 10,000+ monthly plastic credit transactions were achieved by Q4 2025.

• Acceptance Test:

o The platform and blockchain must reflect the monthly transaction count in its reporting dashboard.

4. Manual for Brands to Onboard to Plastiks Platform

• Content Requirements:

o The manual must provide a step-by-step guide for brands to onboard to the Plastiks Platform and be available online on the Plastiks.io website.

• Acceptance Test:

o Guide can be downloaded from Plastiks.io after it has been approved by CEO

5. Converting 10-20% of Brands to Explore Additional Cardano Services

• Content Requirements:

o Achieve this through:

 Webinars: Organize a webinar showcasing Plastiks on Cardano services.

 Post-Webinar Follow-Up: Distribute surveys to assess interest and gather feedback.

 Case Studies and Success Stories: Develop and distribute practical examples of brands successfully using Plastiks on Cardano.

• Acceptance Test:

o The webinar, surveys, and case studies must result in measurable interest from brands.

6. Establishing 2+ Fortune 500 Company Partnerships

• Content Requirements:

o To meet this objective:

 Define criteria for target companies.

 Showcase sustainability dashboards integrating their metrics.

 Develop an engagement plan, including high level proposals and project offers.

 Highlight partnerships through case studies and media content.

• Acceptance Test:

o The partnerships must result in measurable engagement and platform adoption.

7. Creating the Enterprise Adoption Gateway

• Content Requirements:

o Develop a user-friendly interface connecting third-party data on plastic recovery to sustainability dashboards, including:

 Technical integration with third-party databases.

 Comprehensive user documentation.

 Visual diagrams illustrating data flow.

• Acceptance Test:

o Corporate users must confirm that the gateway is functional and easy to use.

8. Amplification Through Brand Partner Networks

• Content Requirements:

o Ensure this deliverable complements brand-led communications by:

 Defining roles for partner networks.

 Developing collaborative campaigns (e.g., webinars, co-branded content).

 Aligning messaging and timing across all network partners.

• Acceptance Test:

o The campaigns must be validated through engagement metrics and feedback.

9. AMA Sessions

• Content Requirements:

o Host AMA sessions in English and Spanish, presenting the Plastiks platform on Cardano.

o Recordings and documented Q&A must be made available for future reference.

• Acceptance Test:

o Participants must confirm that the sessions were informative and engaging.

10. Increasing Institutional Adoption Rates

• Content Requirements:

o Drive institutional adoption by:

 Prioritizing sectors (e.g., consumer goods, food and beverage, technology).

 Providing incentive programs (e.g., free trials, tailored support).

 Hosting thought leadership roundtables.

 Launching targeted outreach campaigns.

• Acceptance Test:

o The adoption metrics must be validated through stakeholder feedback.

11. Measuring Network Effects as Brands Onboard Partners

• Content Requirements:

o Track and present network effects by:

 Defining metrics (e.g., new connections, collaboration frequency).

 Implementing a monitoring tool to visualize network growth.

 Publishing quarterly reports with visualizations.

• Acceptance Test:

o The network growth metrics must be validated through data and stakeholder feedback.

12. Industry Event to Showcase the Platform and Brand Case Studies

• Content Requirements:

o Organize an industry event to showcase the platform and present brand case studies.

• Acceptance Test:

o Video from event will be published on Youtube.

13. Community Event to Showcase the Platform and Celebrate Its Inauguration

• Content Requirements:

o Host a community event to showcase the platform and celebrate its launch.

• Acceptance Test:

o Video from event will be publised on youtube

14. Quarterly Ecosystem Impact Presentations for future reporting

• Content Requirements:

o Create quarterly milestones and deliver presentations with visuals, videos, and Q&A sessions.

• Acceptance Test:

o CEO and COO must confirm that the presentations are informative and engaging and have a standard template approach to retrieving and showing the information related to impact.

15. Full Technical Documentation

• Content Requirements:

o The documentation must outline all development done over the past 12 months.

• Acceptance Test:

o CTO and head of product must confirm that the documentation is correct and that it includes the full scope.

16. 2026 Brand Expansion Strategy

• Content Requirements:

o The strategy must outline how to acquire and onboard 10+ brands over the course of 2026.

• Acceptance Test:

o The strategy must be validated through stakeholder feedback and signed off by the sales manager and CEO

17. Minimum of 4 Brands Actively Using the App

• Content Requirements:

o Evidence must show that 4 brands have profiles and have purchased plastic credits.

• Acceptance Test:

o Dashboard data must confirm the brands’ activity and engagement on the platform.
description:
1. The Close-Out Video and Report

Documented environmental impact metrics from 2025

2. 350,000+ Plastic Credits Transacted  

 Ensure that 350,000+ plastic credits have been transacted on the platform.

3. 10,000 Monthly Plastic Credit Transactions by Q4 2025  

 Achieve 10,000 monthly plastic credit transactions by Q4 2025.

4. Manual for Brands to Onboard to Plastiks Platform  

 Complete and publish the manual for brands to onboard to the Plastiks Platform, available online on the Plastiks.io website.

5. Converting 10-20% of Brands to Explore Additional Cardano Services  

 Achieve this through:  

 a. Webinars: Organize a webinar showcasing Plastiks on Cardano services.  

 b. Post-Webinar Follow-Up: Distribute surveys to assess interest and gather feedback.  

 c. Case Studies and Success Stories: Develop and distribute practical examples of brands successfully using Plastiks on Cardano.

6. Establishing 2+ Fortune 500 Company Partnerships  

 To meet this objective, we will:  

 a. Define Criteria: Identify target companies aligning with Fortune 500 standards and sustainability goals.  

 b. Sustainability Dashboards: Showcase the integration of their sustainability metrics within the Plastiks platform.  

 c. Engagement Plan: Develop an outreach strategy, including personalized proposals, meetings, and pilot project offers.  

 d. Highlight Partnerships: Use case studies and media content to demonstrate the value of these partnerships.

7. Creating the Enterprise Adoption Gateway  

 Develop a user-friendly interface connecting third-party data on plastic recovery to sustainability dashboards. This will involve:  

 a. Technical Integration: Ensure compatibility with various third-party databases and data formats.  

 b. User Documentation: Provide comprehensive guides and tutorials for corporate users.  

 c. Visual Data: Develop clear diagrams illustrating data flow from corporate systems to the Plastiks platform.

8. Amplification Through Brand Partner Networks  

 Ensure this deliverable complements brand-led communications by:  

 a. Defining Roles: Clearly delineate how partner networks amplify messages.  

 b. Collaborative Campaigns: Develop joint campaigns, such as webinars or co-branded content.  

 c. Content Strategy: Align messaging and timing across all network partners for maximum impact.

9 AMA Sessions

1. English AMA Session 

a. An AMA session is scheduled and hosted in English. 

b. The session presents the Plastiks platform on Cardano. 

c. A recording of the session is made available for later viewing. 

d. Key questions and answers are documented for future reference.

2. Spanish AMA Session 

a. An AMA session is scheduled and hosted in Spanish. 

b. The session presents the Plastiks platform on Cardano. 

c. A recording of the session is made available for later viewing. 

d. Key questions and answers are documented for future reference.

10. Increasing Institutional Adoption Rates  

 Drive institutional adoption by:  

 a. Sector Prioritization: Focus on industries such as consumer goods, food and beverage, and technology.  

 b. Incentive Programs: Provide limited-time free trials and tailored support packages for early adopters.  

 c. Thought Leadership: Host roundtable discussions with industry leaders to address adoption barriers.  

 d. Outreach Campaigns: Launch targeted campaigns to communicate the platform’s value proposition.

11. Measuring Network Effects as Brands Onboard Partners  

 Track and present network effects by:  

 a. Defining Metrics: Measure indicators such as new connections formed and collaboration frequency.  

 b. Monitoring Tool: Implement a tracking system to record and visualize network growth.  

 c. Quarterly Reports: Publish updates with visualizations such as network maps and growth charts.

12. Industry Event to Showcase the Platform and Brand Case Studies  

 Organize an industry event to showcase the platform and present brand case studies.

13. Community Event to Showcase the Platform and Celebrate Its Inauguration

 Host a community event to showcase the platform and celebrate its launch.

14. Quarterly Ecosystem Impact Presentations templates for future reporting.

To fulfill this deliverable, we will:

Milestone Planning: Create quarterly milestones that align with key reporting periods:

Q1: Publish an initial report on baseline metrics and early progress.

Q2: Host a webinar to present mid-year achievements and insights.

Q3: Highlight case studies and detailed metrics of success.

Q4: Deliver a final comprehensive report summarizing annual impact.

Interactive Formats: Incorporate visuals, videos, and Q&A sessions to enhance engagement during presentations.

15. Full technical documentation, outlining all development done the past 12 months.

16. 2026 brand expansion strategy, on how to acquire and onboard 10+ brands over the course of 2026

17. Minimum of 4 brands actively using the app, all brands have profiles and have purchased plastic credits.

acceptance_criteria: The criterium for acceptance is that corresponding pull requests are posted on the OpShin and UPLC repository and pass the continuous integration. Further the completion will be publicly shared through our Twitter communication channel (@OpShinDev) and on our Discord server (Opshin Den)
description:
Plutus V3 brings new functions to the UPLC machine. Concretely

  • Sums of Products (CIP 85)
  • BLS, Blake and Keccak crypto primitives (including cryptographic curves)
  • Bitwise primitives (CIP 58)
  • An updated cost mapping to accomodate these new primitives

Our outputs are the implementation of these and testing their correctness using *all* the UPLC conformance tests from the official plutus repository (https://github.com/IntersectMBO/plutus/tree/master/plutus-conformance/test-cases/uplc/evaluation). The repository with the current Plutus V2 implementation and a pending Plutus V1 implementation is publicly accessible here: https://github.com/OpShin/uplc and contains continuous integration and a significant amount of existing test cases which have to pass as well.
title: Implementing main PlutusV3 features in UPLC

acceptance_criteria:
The criterium for acceptance is that corresponding pull requests are posted on the OpShin repository and pass the continuous integration, where applicable. The GitHub repository is https://github.com/OpShin/opshin

Further the completion of this milestone will be publicly communicated through our Twitter and Discord communication channels.
description:
Plutus V3 brings changes to the Smart Contract API in interaction with the blockchain (in particular a changed ScriptContext). The correct representation of the ScriptContext during a transaction is encoded in the corresponding API classes in the OpShin repository.

Our outputs are the implementation of these new ScriptContext classes and 2-3 unit test cases to compare the implementation and its CBOR encoding with CBOR encodings extracted from real transactions on-chain, ensuring that they match the blockchain specification.
title: Implementing new Script Context

acceptance_criteria:
The criteria are 1) new version of OpShin published that features PlutusV3 and 2) transaction on Cardano mainnet that executes an OpShin PlutusV3 contract. The links to each will be shared in this channel.

The tested smart contract(s) on the mainnet clearly demonstrate the specific changes Plutus V3 implements over V2. This includes in particular the spending of funds from a script address without a provided datum (due to the now optional datum). Moreover the change in script cost will be highlighted, which is expected to be largely reduced for bitwise operations.

Moreover the completion of this milestone will be shared through our Twitter and Discord channels.
description:
After the implementation of the new features, we need to merge the changes into the mainstream OpShin implementation, adapt example contracts and test the new features end-to-end on the blockchain and publish a new version of OpShin.

First, this means that the bitwise integer to bytestring (and back) primitives will replace the manual implementation provided for the current implementation.

Secondly, the dual-usage of smart contracts in PlutusV3 is now simplified and its implementation in OpShin will be adapted to handle the single script argument correctly.

The outputs are a new OpShin version, the adaption of all example contracts in the OpShin repository to the new ScriptContext and test contracts executed on the testnet blockchain, in particular at least the vesting and gift contract, which are foundational to smart contract development and introduced in the first 3 weeks of the Plutus Pioneer Program. They interact meaningfully with the Script Context by accessing the list of signatories and time range, and make use of the newly optional script datum. Moreover a specific smart contract that accesses changed parts of the context is developed, accessing fields that are changed in PlutusV3 according to the changelog: https://github.com/IntersectMBO/plutus/blob/master/plutus-ledger-api/CHANGELOG.md#changed-2 and some of the new bitwise and cryptographic features.

The concrete changes will be documented by updating and adding corresponding examples in the example section in the OpShin repository and a description of new primitives and features in the OpShin book (book.opshin.dev).
title: Extensive adaption and testing of OpShin and release of new Version

acceptance_criteria:

The form was shared via social media (Reddit, Twitter, Discord) for at least 2 weeks. The results of a shared form collecting feedback will be shared and proof of discussion of the new features on forums and social media.

description:

Further we will share outputs from the following activities:

  • Collect and analyze feedback from developers to gauge satisfaction and gather insights for further improvements.
  • Interact within the community on forums and social media to evaluate the reception and enthusiasm for the project.

Note that documentation and example scripts will be shared already due to Milestone 3, and only adapted based on feedback received in Milestone 4.

Further we will provide:

  • Final close-out report
  • Final closeout video

The primary acceptance criteria used for the F10 project was the uptime reports as monitored at the following link: https://stats.uptimerobot.com/GJzyBtWA4K

In addition, as per reviewers request, I will provide a video demonstrating the outputs are live as well once per quarter (milestone). This will include visiting each of the relevant pages to demonstrate liveliness as well as visiting the back end systems so the reviewer can see the current node versions.

And finally, as with the F10 project, the reviewer can visit the site at any time to perform their own liveliness check.

  3. Live stake will be working - a test will be developed to compare live stake for a subset of pools against db-sync. Due to complexities of syncronizing live stake to a specific block height between db-sync and pooltool we will analyze a subset of the pools to confirm live stake is working properly. We will do this once per quarter.
  4. Reward data will be up to date - we will demonstrate that reward data is provided for the most recently completed epoch.
  5. PoolTool code will be open source still
  6. Pooltool will be running on the latest node release within 2 weeks of such a release.
  7. Pooltool load time will be under 4 seconds for the main page (https://pooltool.io/) without caching

acceptance_criteria:

description:

acceptance_criteria:
To accept this milestone, the reviewer shall:

  • Confirm that a feature roadmap has been publicly published and all published features align with one or more of the statuses listed above and each feature has been assigned a development phase and estimated time of completion.
  • Confirm that a beta release of the software is publicly available through GitHub Releases (example: v1.0.0-beta)
  • Visit the publicly available beta platform (SaaS) and confirm that features and functionality are working as described in the feature roadmap document (public beta). This must include at least testing implementation versions of all features identified for Public Beta or Public Launch phases of development.
  • Watch the summary video showcasing the feature roadmap and the features described within it, the publicly available SaaS platform, the work that has been done so far on development and testing, and the progress of the marketing strategy.
  • Review the draft/work-in-progress marketing strategy document.
description:
Throughout our closed beta launch several key features were requested and during this milestone we will work to deliver those prior to opening for a public beta release as part of this milestone.

Outputs from this milestone will include:

  • A document describing the features of the software and their state of readiness. Features that are critical for public beta or full public release must be identified in this document. All features must be assigned a phase of development and estimated time of completion such as: Public Beta (03/2025), Public Launch (04/2025), Post Launch (06/2025), Post Launch (Q1 2026). All features must be assigned a status of one of the following:
  • Complete: The feature is incorporated into the software package, has been tested, and is ready for production use.
  • Testing: The feature has been incorporated into the software package but is still undergoing testing and should not be considered ready for production use.
  • Development: The feature is being actively developed during the current phase of development work. Any implemented code is not even ready for testing yet and is not ready for production use.
  • Roadmap: The feature is aligned with the development team's goals and is slated for development during a future development cycle. Items added to the Roadmap should have an anticipated development cycle assigned to them to provide an estimated time of arrival.
  • Proposed: The feature has been proposed but is still under consideration and ideation phase so has not been formally added to a development cycle on the current project roadmap. This status can be considered as a "Feature Wishlist" for future development.
  • A public, beta release of the software that is publicly available and accessible via Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) deployment
  • A publicly accessible GitHub containing the source code of the platform and a beta version has been tagged
  • A video showcasing the current state of the platform and its features
  • A draft/working marketing strategy document
title: Feature Finalization

acceptance_criteria:

  • Review documentation of code coverage and functionality testing and results. Code coverage should include frontend endpoints, backend endpoints, and publicly exposed API endpoints

acceptance_criteria:
The milestone is acceptable if the submitted document contains detailed plans for the software. It should outline:

• Software Stack: The document must specify the software stack to be used, most likely including Python, Node.js, and React. However, this may change depending on internal criteria.

• User Input Collection: The document should explain where user inputs will be collected. Inputs may be gathered through an interface that is either hosted locally or on a web application. The software architecture is most likely intended for a web-based application, but the document should also include notes on how the system would function if run locally.

• Computation Backend: The backend will most likely consist of a collection of Python scripts running locally or on a server to process and provide the required outputs.

• User-Friendly Frontend: The frontend will most likely be developed using React to ensure a smooth and intuitive user experience.

• Integrations with the Xerberus Partner Chain: The software architecture should display several options for utilising the risk protocol engine. These options include running it locally, in the cloud, or directly as a Risk Sub Score on the Xerberus Node. The software architecture plan should reflect these scenarios and the flexibility to use them as needed.

• APIs in the Software Architecture: The architecture must incorporate several APIs. For example, if the solution is not running locally, an API must be included to communicate with the computation backend hosted in the cloud. Additionally, the software must include an API to feed Risk Ratings from Xerberus into the system. This API could retrieve the ratings either from the blockchain or a server backend.

Important: This document serves as a preliminary outline of what is known at this stage. Additional details will be added as the final software architecture takes shape. In case we diverge from any of the outlined points, an explanation will be provided within the submitted milestone to justify the changes. It is important to allow a degree of flexibility, as we might discover more efficient approaches that improve upon our current understanding of the application.

The document must be several pages long to ensure it provides sufficient depth and clarity for the milestone.

description:
Design the user interface and experience for Buriza.Browser, tailored specifically for a browser extension workflow.  

The design will focus on seamless integration of wallet functionalities into the browser, providing intuitive access to Cardano dApps, and transaction management.  

The design will also accommodate users configuring their own backend servers and interacting with decentralized applications directly.  

1. Wireframes and mockups for extension screens will be provided for the following features: 

  • Sending assets: Form for entering recipient address, asset type, and amount 
  • Receiving assets: Any received assets will reflect and display in the wallet balance and asset list once the transaction is confirmed on the blockchain 
  • Viewing balance and assets: Shows an overview of the wallet's current balance, list of assets held, and their respective values 
  • Transaction history: List of past transactions, filtered or sorted by date, asset type, or transaction status for the specific wallet address 
  • Full node setup: Step-by-step process for configuring a backend server or full node 
  • dApp access: Embedded interface for connecting with other Cardano decentralized applications 

2. A comprehensive document report covering the following: 

  • Design decisions: Visual hierarchy (fonts, colors, iconography and UI elements), intuitive navigation, and consistency across screens for predictable user experience. 
  • Usability considerations: Simplified workflows for common actions such as sending and receiving assets and guided wallet setup for first-time users. 
  • Browser extension-specific accessibility features: Customizable interface options.

description:
Note: Buriza.Core is a separate project and a proposed library that was not funded but will still be developed by the company. It can be seen here: https://cardano.ideascale.com/c/cardano/idea/128091  

It will serve as the core library for Buriza, shared across the desktop, mobile, and browser versions. Buriza.Core will provide essential functionalities, such as sending transactions and managing wallets, to power the Buriza ecosystem. 

1. Integration of Buriza.Core Functionalities into Buriza.Browser 

Integrate Buriza.Core functionalities into Buriza.Browser, ensuring smooth interaction between the extension and Buriza.Core’s API.  

The focus will be on: 

  • Providing secure, decentralized access to Cardano dApps 
  • Enabling users to configure their own servers 
  • Building and signing transactions 
  • Managing assets directly through the browser extension.  

The integration will allow Buriza.Browser to offer robust Cardano wallet features while operating entirely within the browser environment.  

Deliverables

1. Updated source code with Buriza.Core functionalities integrated into the browser extension. 

  • Smooth data flow between the extension interface and blockchain data.

description:
SDK, and a How-To guide on wrapping an existing service with Subbit.xyz

M2 Tx building outputs components of managing a subbit channel.

M3 extends M2 output with a set of functions and/or services that facilitate the integration of subbit ie a subbit SDK.

**An appropriate form this takes is not yet known.**

Both client and server (ie consumer and provider) require persistent state including signing keys, and an l1 interface for monitoring channels as well as building and submitting txs. There is not a one-size-fits-all answer to this since it depends on the execution context for each.

We presume that the client and server interact via http requests (although the core of subbit is agnostic to transport. Snail mail would also work). Perhaps subbit can act as "middleware" both sides leaving the application otherwise untouched. However it is likely that for only the most basic applications (eg where the cost of a request can be deduced by regex on the url) will the application and costings be so decoupled.

The term "SDK" is, on reflection, suboptimal. There is no compiler, which according to various blogs is a typical part of what forms an SDK. However, neither "API" nor "library" quite encompassed this "piece".

We propose 2 outputs:

1- A (sub)repo of "code to facilitate subbit integration"

2- A demo app with both client and server executables which can be run with optional subbit.

This makes use of the first output.

When run without subbit, the server has the following API:

* now - returns current time

* put(key, val) - puts (key,val) in persistent storage

* get(key) - gets val by key or reports none.

The client can query these freely. There is a script that demonstrates these being done.

When run with subbit, the api is appropriately wrapped so that each request must have a subbit IOU.

Moreover the API is extended with the necessary end points for ergonomic subbit usage, for example the terms of service.

There is a script demonstrating a full lifecycle. This can be run with both with a faux L1 interface or a testnet / mainnet.

There is a script demonstrating an "evil" client and an "evil" server.
title: "SDK" + example

description:
Orcfax integration: payment solution based on Subbit

Orcfax is an oracle service provider for the cardano blockchain. Orcfax clients are typically dapps. They request oracle data, aka fact statements, to be made available on the Cardano blockchain.

Typically the relationship reflects that appropriate to Subbit: there is a consumer and a provider in which the consumer is repeatedly making small requests of service over a period of time.

The output is real world application using subbit.

A client can:

* view channel state and manage channel (ie open, fund, close, drain).

* place orders for fact statements

* see historical orders.

A provider can:

* view subscriber channels

* handle orders.

It is likely the output has components that are web based guis, although we reserve the option to use a cli based interface if its deemed more appropriate.

Open sourcing the Orcfax integration as a real world application.

This is not just: change repo setting, git add OS license.

Open sourcing includes that, but is really about making the code accessible to any interested party.

The readme will outline the overall repo layout, and the pre-req dependencies (eg `node + vite`), and the key commands for building, testing and running (eg `pnpm i && pnpm test && pnpm server`).

It will also contain an explanation of expected resources and how to acquire/ run them (eg blockfrost key, ogmios/kupo) and signposting to where a user can find out more about these.

The output includes a blog post-esque piece that introduces and tours the code.

The piece contains reflects on the design decisions made (in place of any more formal ADR) and comments on possible alternatives and extensions.

  3. Stakeholder Approval: Approved and signed off by both Optim Labs and Switzerland for UNHCR, providing a deep dive into the platform’s end-to-end architecture.
  4. Risk Assessment Framework
  5. Overview of Protocol Risks and Donation Yield Module Risks: Provides complete description of protocol mechanics that power the concentration of yield, including the exposure as the junior tranche in the system and the potential buffer for AMO losses or underperforming strategies.
  6. Public Documentation Repository

description:
Develop a comprehensive system design specification that defines the core architectural framework, functional modules, and operational workflows of the OToken Donation Platform. These materials will form the foundation for both smart contract development and the off-chain infrastructure necessary to implement the protocol.


  1. Technical System Design Specification
  2. Blueprint for On-Chain and Off-Chain Components: A detailed breakdown of the protocol architecture, including system components, data flow, and interactions.
  3. Core Functionalities: Clear delineation of essential elements, such as the Strategy Vault, donation mechanics, and yield distribution logic.
  4. Risk Assessment Framework
  5. Document outlining the application’s risk/reward dynamics that create the additional yield 
  6. Public Documentation Repository
  7. User-Friendly, Open-Access Materials: Documentation that translates the technical specification into non-technical terms.
  8. Guides and Examples: Step-by-step instructions, illustrative examples, and best practices for using the OToken Donation Platform’s features.
  9. ﻿Key Workflows: In-depth explanations of critical processes like minting Participation NFTs, directing donations to the yield-generating vault, and performing administrative tasks.

  3. Alignment with Milestone 1: Code structured to reflect the architectural principles laid out in the original system design specification.
  4. Validation: Demonstrations on the Cardano testnet or mainnet beta confirming that yield distribution and NFT minting function correctly (e.g., transferring funds, minting tokens).
  5. Code Walkthrough Video
  6. Architectural Overview: A lead developer presentation showcasing how the contracts align with the previously approved system design. Test transaction history walkthrough will be provided.

description:
Implement the fundamental on-chain components of the OToken Donation Platform, building upon the technical specifications outlined in Milestone 1. During this phase, the Strategy Vault, Donation/Yield Distribution Module, and NFT Minting Module will be developed and demonstrated via testnet or beta mainnet deployments.

  1. Core Smart Contract Implementation
  2. Strategy Vault (Staked OToken): Manages staked OTOKEN and leverages internal or external yield strategies to grow donated assets. Integrates with external protocols handling yield generation (manual or automated) as per system design.
  3. Donation/Yield Distribution Module: Receives donations in OTOKEN (or other configured assets) and orchestrates yield distribution among designated beneficiaries. Ensures accurate allocation of generated yield from the Strategy Vault, preserving transparency and auditability.
  4. NFT Minting Module: On-chain mechanism for minting NFTs that acknowledge user contributions. Defines metadata standards and minting conditions in line with the system design.
  5. ﻿﻿Code Walkthrough Video
  6. Video of code walkthrough to describe the smart contract mechanism and working live interactions of a private testnet or limited mainnet deployment for non-technical Milestone Reviewers and the broader Catalyst community to understand the scope of the system.
